嘉靖二十三年進士登科錄

玉音

嘉靖二十三年三月初九日，禮部尚書兼翰林院學士臣張璧等於奉天門奏為科舉事：「會試天下舉人，取中三百二十名。本年三月十五日殿試，合擬讀卷官及執事等官，少保兼太子太保、禮部尚書、武英殿大學士嚴嵩等六十三員。其進士出身等第，恭依太祖高皇帝欽定資格：第一甲例取三名，第一名從六品，第二、第三名正七品，賜進士及第；第二甲從七品，賜進士出身；第三甲正八品，賜同進士出身。」奉聖旨：「是。」欽此。

讀卷官

光祿大夫、柱國、少保兼太子太保、禮部尚書、武英殿大學士嚴嵩〔乙丑進士〕。
光祿大夫、柱國、少保兼太子太保、吏部尚書許讚〔丙辰進士〕。
榮祿大夫、太子太保、兵部尚書毛伯溫〔戊辰進士〕。
translation_en:
Record of Metropolitan Graduates (jinshi) of the Twenty-third Year of Jiajing (1544)

The Imperial Voice

On the ninth day of the third month of the twenty-third year of Jiajing, your servant Zhang Bi, Minister of Rites concurrently serving as Academician of the Hanlin Academy, and others memorialized at Fengtian Gate concerning the civil-service examinations:

“In the Metropolitan Examination of provincial graduates from throughout the empire, 320 candidates were selected. For the Palace Examination on the fifteenth day of the third month of this year, we duly propose sixty-three officials as Examination Readers and other functionaries, including Yan Song, Junior Guardian, concurrently Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Rites, and Grand Secretary of the Hall of Military Glory.

“The distinctions in status conferred upon the metropolitan graduates shall respectfully follow the qualifications imperially established by Emperor Taizu Gao. In the first class, three candidates shall be selected according to precedent: the first shall receive lower sixth rank, and the second and third shall receive upper seventh rank, with all three granted the status of ‘metropolitan graduate with honors.’ Those in the second class shall receive lower seventh rank and be granted the status of ‘metropolitan graduate.’ Those in the third class shall receive upper eighth rank and be granted the status of ‘equivalent to metropolitan graduate.’”

The imperial rescript was received: “Approved.” Respectfully received.

Examination Readers

Yan Song was Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Pillar of State, Junior Guardian, concurrently Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Rites, and Grand Secretary of the Hall of Military Glory. 〔Metropolitan graduate of the yichou year.〕

Xu Zan was Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Pillar of State, Junior Guardian, concurrently Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and Minister of Personnel. 〔Metropolitan graduate of the bingchen year.〕

Mao Bowen was Grand Master for Glorious Happiness, Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and Minister of War. 〔Metropolitan graduate of the wuchen year.〕

translation_en:
Sequence of Imperial Favors and Honors

On the morning of the fifteenth day of the third month of the twenty-third year of Jiajing (1544), the tribute scholars proceeded to the inner palace for the Palace Examination. The emperor took his seat in Fengtian Hall and personally bestowed the policy question.

On the morning of the nineteenth day of the third month, all civil and military officials attended in their court robes, standing in their assigned ranks. That day, the Embroidered-uniform Guard arrayed the imperial ceremonial equipage on the vermilion steps and in the vermilion courtyard. The emperor took his seat in Fengtian Hall. Officials of the Court of State Ceremonial transmitted the imperial decree and called out the candidates’ names. Officials of the Ministry of Rites carried the yellow list of successful candidates, led by drums and music, out through Chang’an Left Gate. Once the list had been posted outside the gate, officials of Shuntian Prefecture escorted the first-ranked graduate (zhuangyuan) back to his residence with parasols, canopies, and a ceremonial retinue.

On the second day of the fourth month …

On the fifth day of the fourth month, court robes, a cap, and a girdle were bestowed upon the first-ranked graduate, and paper currency upon the metropolitan graduates (jinshi).

translation_en:
First Class: three men, granted the distinction of metropolitan graduate with honors (jinshi jidi).

Qin Minglei 秦鳴雷 was registered in Linhai County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a military household. He was an added-quota student of the prefectural school and specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Ziyu; he ranked fourth in his family and was twenty-seven years old, born on the second day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Zongfu; his grandfather, Yanbin, received the honorary appointment of Vice Director of the Office of Messengers and the posthumous appointment of Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice. His father, Wen, was Left Administration Vice Commissioner in a Provincial Administration Commission. His mother, née Yao, was granted the title Lady of Suitability; his stepmother was née Yang. His father was deceased and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Mingchun, a tribute scholar; Mingxia, Right Mentor of the Right Spring Office and concurrently Senior Compiler of the Hanlin Academy; and Mingqiu. His younger brother was Mingdong. He married a woman née Zhao. He placed eightieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 107th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qu Jingchun 瞿景淳 was registered in Changshu County, Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili, in an artisan household. He was a student of the county school and specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shidao; he ranked first in his family and was thirty-eight years old, born on the twenty-seventh day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Qin; his grandfather, Pin; his father, Guoxian; and his mother, née Qin. His father was deceased and his mother was living. He married a woman née Li. He placed sixteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Qing 吳情 was registered in Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, Zhili, in a military household. He was a student of the National University and specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yizhong; he ranked first in his family and was forty-one years old, born on the twelfth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Guan; his grandfather, Cheng; his father, Heng; and his mother, née Xu. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Huai, Xing, Heng, Chen, and Dun. He married a woman née Yang and subsequently a woman née Dai. He placed twelfth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventy-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

熊逵〔貫江西臨江府清江縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字于漸，行五，年三十四，十月二十日生〕。曾祖可昂，祖春和，父愛，母彭氏。具慶下，兄運、逢，弟造，娶楊氏。江西鄉試第十八名，會試第一百九十五名。

戴完〔貫直隸安慶府桐城縣，民籍，縣學生，治書經，字仲修，行五，年二十六，二月二十七日生〕。曾祖冕〔歲貢監生〕，祖寶，父儒〔義官〕，母劉氏，繼母余氏。具慶下，兄元、充，弟克、覺，娶吳氏，繼娶方氏。應天府鄉試第九十一名，會試第二百四十五名。
translation_en:
Second Class: ninety-three men, granted the status of metropolitan graduate (jinshi).

Tu Xuan, a native of Fengcheng County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was registered in a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Tingju; he ranked eighth among his brothers and was thirty-five years old, born on the third day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gujian, his grandfather Zhixun, and his father Chaoning; his mother was née Xiong. His father was living and his mother deceased. He married a woman née Zuo. He placed forty-fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and forty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xiong Kui, a native of Qingjiang County, Linjiang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was registered in a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Yujian; he ranked fifth among his brothers and was thirty-four years old, born on the twentieth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ke'ang, his grandfather Chunhe, and his father Ai; his mother was née Peng. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yun and Feng, and his younger brother was Zao. He married a woman née Yang. He placed eighteenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 195th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dai Wan, a native of Tongcheng County, Anqing Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was registered in a civilian household and was a county school student. He specialized in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Zhongxiu; he ranked fifth among his brothers and was twenty-six years old, born on the twenty-seventh day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Mian, a student of the Directorate of Education admitted through the annual tribute quota; his grandfather was Bao, and his father Ru, an honorary official. His mother was née Liu, and his stepmother née Yu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yuan and Chong, and his younger brothers were Ke and Jue. He married a woman née Wu and subsequently a woman née Fang. He placed ninety-first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 245th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Lin Zhu, registered in a civilian household in Wendeng County, Ninghai Subprefecture, Dengzhou Prefecture, Shandong, was a county government student. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Kongyuan. First in birth order, he was thirty years old and was born on the twentieth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jun, his grandfather Zhong, and his father Yong, a Sacrificial Attendant. His mother and stepmother were both née Jiang. Both parents were deceased. His wife was née Zhang. He placed fifty-ninth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 190th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Que, registered in a civilian household in Wan’an County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Zhiqing. Second in birth order, he was thirty-seven years old and was born on the tenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather Guangheng was Grand Master for Fostering Goodness and Minister of Justice. His grandfather Qiao was Left Provincial Administration Commissioner, posthumously granted the rank of Grand Master for Thorough Counsel. His father Yu was formerly Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Left Vice Minister of Justice. His father’s previous wife, née Xiao, was posthumously granted the title Lady of Gentleness; his mother, née Wang, was granted the same title. His mother alone survived. His elder brother Xian was an Office Manager in the Censorate, and his younger brother Qian was a student admitted by virtue of an official’s status. His wife was née Zeng. He placed nineteenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 102nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jiang Bin, registered in an artisan household in Linhai County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a county government student. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Ruguan. First in birth order, he was thirty-three years old and was born on the twenty-second day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lun, his grandfather Ying, and his father Yi. His father’s previous wife was née Peng, and his mother was née Yang. His father alone survived. His younger brothers were Xuan and Hong. His wife was née Hou; he subsequently married a woman née Xie. He placed fifty-ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 246th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Shiyuan, registered in a civilian household in Kunshan County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a native of Wu County and a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Boyun. First in birth order, he was thirty-two years old and was born on the eleventh day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yong, his grandfather Ze, his father Gao, and his mother née Tu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Bing, Shilong, and Can. His wife was née Jin. He placed 110th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Li Yi, registered in a civilian household in Wuqiao County, Jingzhou, Hejian Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the National University specializing in the Book of Poetry; his courtesy name was Meiqing, he ranked twenty-ninth among his male siblings and cousins, and he was aged twenty-nine, born on the twenty-eighth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Xing; his grandfather, Min, and father, Shun, both held honorary offices bestowed for longevity; his mother was née Yu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Shi, a Sacrificial Attendant; Shangjiong and Shangren, both annual tribute students; Tong, a tribute scholar; Dong, a National University student; Wenxue; and Wenju. He married a woman née Liang. He placed seventy-second in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 152nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Shizuo, registered in a civilian household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the National University specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Ruliang, he ranked twenty-eighth among his male siblings and cousins, and he was aged thirty, born on the twelfth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Ding, an Administrator; his grandfather was Wu; his father was Xun; and his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Shiyou, Shiqiao, and Shilun. He married a woman née Wang. He placed ninetieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Song, registered in an artisan household in Xinyu County, Linjiang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a county government school student specializing in the Book of Poetry; his courtesy name was Ruzhen, he ranked seventh among his male siblings and cousins, and he was aged twenty-nine, born on the sixth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Su; his grandfather was Jin; his father was Jun, who held an honorary office bestowed for longevity; and his mother was née Xi. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Gui. He married a woman née Fu and subsequently a woman née Zhang. He placed eighteenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and eighteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Zhichen, registered in a civilian household in She County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the National University specializing in the Book of Poetry; his courtesy name was Weizhong, he ranked third among his male siblings and cousins, and he was aged thirty-five, born on the fifteenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Xian; his grandfather was Fuzong; his father was Shang; and his mother was née Fang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Boshou, and his younger brother was Zhizi. He married a woman née Wang. He placed sixtieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 160th in the Metropolitan Examination.

山東鄉試第七十三名　會試第四十一名
punctuated:
陳天祐〔貫山西澤州，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字謙甫，行二，年三十六，正月初九日生〕。曾祖林，祖秀〔典史〕，父珏〔典史〕，母裴氏。慈侍下，兄仁、儒、偉，弟俊、僑、傑、修、信，娶張氏。山西鄉試第十一名，會試第一百十六名。

許應亨〔貫浙江杭州府錢塘縣，民籍，順天府東安縣人，縣學增廣生，治易經，字子嘉，行九，年三十九，十月十七日生〕。曾祖九臯，祖紳，父龜年〔贈奉直大夫、工部員外郎〕，母陳氏〔封太宜人〕。慈侍下，兄應爵、應元〔工部虞衡司郎中〕、應亨、應期，弟德高、嶽、應奎、應斗、參，娶張氏。順天府鄉試第九十九名，會試第一百四十三名。

謝彬〔貫福建漳州府龍溪縣，民籍，府學附學生，治易經，字文華，行一，年三十一，十二月十一日生〕。曾祖興邦，祖崇顯，父正雄，母林氏。慈侍下，弟彭、彩、彥，娶方氏。福建鄉試第九十名，會試第二百十一名。

許用中〔貫山東兖州府東平州東阿縣，軍籍，縣學增廣生，治書經，字子執，行一，年二十八，十一月初九日生〕。曾祖純，祖汝聰〔監生〕，父東陽，嫡母周氏，繼母孔氏，生母王氏。慈侍下，弟黃中，娶楊氏。山東鄉試第七十三名，會試第四十一名。
translation_en:
Chen Tianyou, registered in Zezhou, Shanxi, in a civilian household, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Qianfu, he ranked second in his family, and he was thirty-six years old, born on the ninth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lin; his grandfather Xiu and father Jue both served as Clerks; his mother was née Pei. His father was deceased and his mother living; his elder brothers were Ren, Ru, and Wei, and his younger brothers Jun, Qiao, Jie, Xiu, and Xin. His wife was née Zhang. He placed eleventh in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 116th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Yingheng, registered in Qiantang County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household, and a native of Dong’an County, Shuntian Prefecture, was an additional student of the county school specializing in the Classic of Changes; his courtesy name was Zijia, he ranked ninth in his family, and he was thirty-nine years old, born on the seventeenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jiugao, his grandfather Shen, and his father Guinian, posthumously awarded the titles Grand Master for Uprightness and Vice Director in the Ministry of Works; his mother, née Chen, was granted the title of Grand Lady of Suitability. His father was deceased and his mother living; his elder brothers are listed as Yingjue, Yingyuan (Director of the Bureau of Forestry and Crafts in the Ministry of Works), Yingheng [?—the candidate’s own name is repeated here], and Yingqi; his younger brothers are listed as Degao, Yue, Yingkui, Yingdou, and Can [?—the division of these names is uncertain]. His wife was née Zhang. He placed ninety-ninth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 143rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xie Bin, registered in Longxi County, Zhangzhou Prefecture, Fujian, in a civilian household, was an attached student of the prefectural school specializing in the Classic of Changes; his courtesy name was Wenhua, he ranked first in his family, and he was thirty-one years old, born on the eleventh day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xingbang, his grandfather Chongxian, his father Zhengxiong, and his mother née Lin. His father was deceased and his mother living; his younger brothers were Peng, Cai, and Yan. His wife was née Fang. He placed ninetieth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 211th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Yongzhong, registered in Dong’e County, Dongping Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, in a military household, was an additional student of the county school specializing in the Classic of Documents; his courtesy name was Zizhi, he ranked first in his family, and he was twenty-eight years old, born on the ninth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chun; his grandfather Rucong was a student of the Directorate of Education; his father was Dongyang. His legal mother was née Zhou, his stepmother née Kong, and his birth mother née Wang. His father was deceased and his mother living; his younger brother was Huangzhong, and his wife was née Yang. He placed seventy-third in the Shandong Provincial Examination and forty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

陳臯謨〔貫直隸常州府江陰縣，民籍，縣學增廣生，治易經，字思賛，行一，年四十，二月二十六日生〕。曾祖至中〔七品散官〕，祖慶〔七品散官〕，父魯，母盛氏。慈侍下，弟益謨，娶華氏。應天府鄉試第一百十七名，會試第一百六十九名。

雷夢麟〔貫江西南昌府進賢縣，民籍，縣學附學生，治書經，字伯仁，行二，年三十一，十月初十日生〕。曾祖仲迅，祖宣，父倫，母朱氏。具慶下，弟夢熊、夢龍、夢鸞，娶萬氏。江西鄉試第六十二名，會試第二十四名。

汪垍〔貫直隸徽州府休寧縣，軍籍，國子生，治書經，字仲弘，行二，年三十四，正月初七日生〕。曾祖武貴，祖齊，父昱〔訓導〕，前母吴氏，母戴氏。重慶下，兄培，弟埇，娶王氏，繼娶張氏。應天府鄉試第九十三名，會試第一百三十七名。
translation_en:
Ruan E, registered in Tongcheng County, Anqing Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Yingjian, and he ranked sixth among his brothers. He was thirty-four, born on the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yongcheng; his grandfather, Xian; and his father, Tingzan, who held an honorary title granted for longevity. His mother was née Wu, and his birth mother was née Zhang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother Peng was a student of the Directorate of Education. He married a woman née Zhang and subsequently a woman née Cheng. He placed forty-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 199th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Gaomo, registered in Jiangyin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was an added student of the county Confucian school. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Sizan, and he ranked first among his brothers. He was forty, born on the twenty-sixth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather Zhizhong and grandfather Qing both held seventh-rank prestige titles. His father was Lu, and his mother was née Sheng. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His younger brother was Yimo. He married a woman née Hua. He placed 117th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 169th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lei Menglin, registered in Jinxian County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was an attached student of the county Confucian school. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Boren, and he ranked second among his brothers. He was thirty-one, born on the tenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhongxun; his grandfather, Xuan; his father, Lun; and his mother, née Zhu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Mengxiong, Menglong, and Mengluan. He married a woman née Wan. He placed sixty-second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and twenty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Ji, registered in Xiuning County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Zhonghong, and he ranked second among his brothers. He was thirty-four, born on the seventh day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wugui; his grandfather, Qi; and his father, Yu, an Assistant Instructor. His father's former wife was née Wu, and his mother was née Dai. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brother was Pei, and his younger brother was Yong. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently a woman née Zhang. He placed ninety-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 137th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wu Guifang, courtesy name Zishi, was registered in a military household in Xinjian County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi. A county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first among his brothers and was twenty-four years old, born on the third day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shixiong; his grandfather was Ke, a provincial sacrificial official; and his father was Shan. His father's former wife was née Ye, his mother née Shu, and his stepmother née Pan. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Jifang, and his wife was née Cui. He placed second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 213th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Xun, courtesy name Ziyi, was registered in a civilian household in Xinjian County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi. A county school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked tenth among his brothers and was twenty-seven years old, born on the twenty-third day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shizhong, his grandfather Wenzheng, his father Suduan, and his mother née Cheng. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Da, Dao, Xuan, Feng, Qian (a secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of War), Xia, Tong, Shu, Di, and Xian; his younger brothers were Yu (an Imperial University student), Zun, Yun, and Kui. His wife was née Kong. He placed fifty-third in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 244th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zha Maochang, courtesy name Yunyan, was registered with the Imperial Medical Office and was a native of Changzhou County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-nine years old, born on the fifteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather Wen was a prefectural vice prefect, posthumously granted the rank of Grand Master of the Palace and the office of Right Administration Vice Commissioner; his grandfather Xun received successive posthumous grants of that rank and office. His father Yingchen was an assistant instructor. His mother was née Chen, and his stepmothers were née Sun and née Lei. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Maoguang (formerly a secretary in the Ministry of Justice), Maozhao (a Metropolitan Examination graduate), Maoqin, Maofang, Maoxian, and Maoyuan. His wife was née Xu. He placed seventy-ninth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 239th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Luo Yiluan, courtesy name Yingzhou, was registered in a civilian household in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian. An additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked fourth among his brothers and was thirty-four years old, born on the seventh day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qi, his grandfather Kuang, and his father Weiyuan, a school instructor. His father's former wife was née Chen, and his mother was née Zeng. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Yifeng, and his wife was née Fang. He placed thirty-fifth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 202nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

馮有年〔貫直隸常州府無錫縣軍籍，國子生，治書經，字子占，行二，年四十五，十月初一日生〕。曾祖以順，祖緒，父季貴，母周氏。慈侍下，兄文富，弟霖，娶周氏，繼娶謝氏、張氏。應天府鄉試第一百二十四名，會試第一百三名。

徐惟賢〔貫浙江紹興府上虞縣民籍，國子生，治易經，字師聖，行一，年三十四，六月初一日生〕。曾祖梗，祖子淪〔恩例冠帶〕，父大中，母張氏，繼母楊氏。具慶下，弟惟能、惟德、惟聰、惟明、惟睿、惟智，娶莊氏。浙江鄉試第七十一名，會試第二百七十六名。
translation_en:
Yu Yipeng, courtesy name Chaoju, was registered in a military household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian; he was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry, fourth in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the sixth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yinbin; his grandfather, Yonghe, received successive posthumous grants of the honorary title Zhongxian dafu and the office of Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud; his father, Zan, held the honorary title Yazhong dafu and served as Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud; and his mother, née Yao, received successive grants of the title Lady of Respect (gongren). His mother was living and his father deceased; his elder brothers were Yikui, Yilong, and Yi'e, and his wife was née Chen. He placed eighty-seventh in the Fujian Provincial Examination and one hundred forty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Guangji, courtesy name Xianqian, was registered in a civilian household in Jiangyin County, Changzhou Prefecture, directly administered territory, and was a native of Jingjiang County; he was an additional student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Classic of Changes, first in birth order, aged twenty-five, and born on the twentieth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yi, his grandfather He, his father Xu, and his mother née Zheng. Both parents were living; his younger brothers were Guangheng, Guanghua, Guangguo, and Guangzhao, and his wife was née Lü. He placed sixty-seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and two hundred ninety-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Feng Younian, courtesy name Zizhan, was registered in a military household in Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, directly administered territory; he was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Documents, second in birth order, aged forty-five, and born on the first day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yishun, his grandfather Xu, his father Jigui, and his mother née Zhou. His mother was living and his father deceased; his elder brother was Wenfu and his younger brother Lin. His first wife was née Zhou, and his subsequent wives were née Xie and née Zhang. He placed one hundred twenty-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and one hundred third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Weixian, courtesy name Shisheng, was registered in a civilian household in Shangyu County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang; he was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Changes, first in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the first day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Geng; his grandfather, Zilun, was authorized to wear official cap and girdle under provisions for imperial favor; his father was Dazhong, his mother née Zhang, and his stepmother née Yang. Both parents were living; his younger brothers were Weineng, Weide, Weicong, Weiming, Weirui, and Weizhi, and his wife was née Zhuang. He placed seventy-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and two hundred seventy-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

季德甫〔貫直隸蘇州府太倉州匠籍，國子生，治易經，字仲修，行二，年三十七，八月二十七日生〕。曾祖讓，祖鑑〔壽官〕，父沐，前母薛氏，母朱氏。具慶下，兄德英，弟鴻磐、孔陽、孔固，娶張氏。應天府鄉試第一百二名，會試第二百二十五名。

戈九章〔貫錦衣衛匠籍，直隸吳縣人，國子生，治禮記，字惟衷，行三，年三十二，十月初六日生〕。曾祖寧，祖瑀，父裕〔鴻臚寺司賓署署丞〕，母雷氏。具慶下，兄九功、九成、九德，弟九儀、九疇〔貢士〕、九經，娶葉氏，繼娶桂氏。順天府鄉試第四十八名，會試第一百七十四名。
translation_en:
Wang Zongyao, registered in a salt-producing household in Fushun County, Xuzhou Prefecture, Sichuan, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Jianfu, he ranked second in birth order, and he was aged forty, born on the sixth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Dabin, his grandfather Pin, and his father Chufeng; his mother was née Ou, and his stepmothers were née Zeng and née Zhang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Zongwu and his younger brother Zongde. He married a woman née Liu, then successively women née Yang 羊 and Yang 楊. He placed thirty-ninth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 270th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Feng Xiong, registered in a civilian household in Jinhua County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Boxiang, he ranked forty-fifth in birth order, and he was aged thirty-two, born on the nineteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather Jie was Surveillance Commissioner in a Provincial Surveillance Commission, advanced to the prestige title Grand Master of Central Service; his grandfather Yang was a District Magistrate, posthumously granted the title of Secretary; and his father Zhu was a Department Magistrate and formerly a Vice Director. His father's former wife, née Zhang, was posthumously granted the title Lady of Peace (anren), and his mother, née Sima, was granted the same title. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Pin, a District Magistrate; Ke, a Department Magistrate; Long; Shan; Xun; Pei; Hu; Xie; and Hua. His younger brother was Peng, and he married a woman née Bai. He placed thirty-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 111th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ji Defu, registered in an artisan household in Taicang Subprefecture, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Zhongxiu, he ranked second in birth order, and he was aged thirty-seven, born on the twenty-seventh day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Rang, his grandfather Jian held an honorary official title bestowed for longevity, and his father was Mu; his father's former wife was née Xue, and his mother was née Zhu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Deying, and his younger brothers were Hongpan, Kongyang, and Konggu. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed 102nd in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 225th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ge Jiuzhang, registered in an artisan household under the Embroidered-Uniform Guard and a native of Wu County in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Weizhong, he ranked third in birth order, and he was aged thirty-two, born on the sixth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Ning, his grandfather Yu 瑀, and his father Yu 裕, Deputy Director of the Office of Receptions in the Court of State Ceremonial; his mother was née Lei. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jiugong, Jiucheng, and Jiude; his younger brothers were Jiuyi, Jiuchou, a Metropolitan Examination graduate (gongshi), and Jiujing. He married a woman née Ye and subsequently a woman née Gui. He placed forty-eighth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 174th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Liu Lun 劉崙, courtesy name Shanfu, was registered in Wuwei Subprefecture, Luzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region, in a military household. A student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Book of Odes, he was third in family order, aged twenty-seven, and born on the fourth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kegong; his grandfather, Chen, held a seventh-rank prestige title; his father, Kai, held the honorary title of Official for Righteousness; and his mother was née Lin. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Zu, and his younger brothers were Hui and Song. His wife was née Hou. He placed sixtieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 193rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Aimin 林愛民, courtesy name Weimu, was registered in Funing Subprefecture, Fujian, in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Rites, he was eighth in family order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the twenty-sixth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Teng; his grandfather, Wenmeng, was a tribute scholar; his father was Kuang, and his mother was née Sheng. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Shi and Liang. His wife was née Huang; he subsequently married women née Hu and née Chen. He placed tenth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and sixty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zeng Chu 曽楚, courtesy name Weiqiao, was registered in Nanhai County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, in a civilian household. An additional student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in family order, aged thirty, and born on the second day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Guangji; his grandfather was Kai; his father was Qing, and his mother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Qi, and his younger brother was Han. His wife was née Huang. He placed twenty-fourth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and seventieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xie Mengjin 謝孟金, courtesy name Zichun, was registered in the Central Battalion of the Chenzhou Guard, Henan, in a military household. A student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was third in family order, aged thirty, and born on the twenty-first day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wang; his grandfather was Peng; his father was Rang; his father's former wife was née Li, and his mother was née Qiao. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Yu and Mengyang, and his younger brother was Mengchen. His wife was née Qi; he subsequently married a woman née Lou. He placed fourth in the Henan Provincial Examination and ninety-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Fang Yu, registered in a civilian household in She County, Huizhou Prefecture, directly administered by the central government, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Yuanzhong; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged forty, born on the twenty-ninth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Yanrong, his grandfather Liuzong, and his father Congzheng; his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Xiang, Bi, Guan, Rui, Qi, Yu, Zhen, and Chen. His wife was née Song. He placed fifty-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 215th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hong Gongxie, registered in a civilian household in Longxi County, Zhangzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was an added-quota student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Tinghe; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty, born on the eighteenth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Ming, posthumously appointed Investigating Censor; his grandfather was Yi, Left Assistant Administration Commissioner in the Provincial Administration Commission; and his father was Yuerui. His mother was née Shen. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Yitai, Yiqing, Gongliang, Gongxun, Gongzan, Gongjin, Gongzhi, and Gonge. His wife was née Su. He placed twelfth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and forty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Zhu, registered in a civilian household in Xiaoshan County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Ruyu; he ranked third among his brothers and was aged thirty, born on the seventh day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Jiang, posthumously awarded the title Grand Master for Assisting in Governance and appointed Right Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate; his grandfather was Shan, an honorary official recognized for longevity; and his father was Yi. His father's principal wife was née Shi, his stepmother née Yu, and his birth mother née Chen. His father was living, his mother deceased. His elder brother was Deng and his younger brother Mu. His wife was née Wo. He placed eighty-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and sixtieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jiang Mian, registered in a civilian household in Nanfeng County, Jianchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Duanfu; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-five, born on the tenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Jinglun, his grandfather Bingzhao, an honorary official recognized for longevity, and his father Zhou. His mother was née Li and his stepmother née Huang. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brother was Tan. His wife was née Zhu; he was subsequently betrothed to a woman née Ma. He placed forty-fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and eighty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Tao Dayou, registered in a civilian household in Kuaiji County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a county school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Ziqian; he ranked seventh among his brothers and was aged thirty-four, born on the nineteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xing, a tribute student; his grandfather was Gao, a county magistrate; his father was Shiwen, a county magistrate; and his mother was née Yang. He had grandparents and parents living. His elder brothers were Dajing, a provincial sacrificial official (shengjiguan), Dalun, and Daben, a student of the Imperial University. His younger brothers were Dayou [?—the same name as the candidate], a provincial sacrificial official; Dafeng, an office assistant in the Court of Imperial Entertainments; and Daguan, Dalin, Dazhang, Dazhong, Dashou, Dacheng, Dafang, Dalu, Dafan, and Dajian. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently another woman née Wang. He placed forty-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fifty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Wei held official household registration in the Embroidered-uniform Guard and was a native of Pinghu County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. He was a probationary Secretariat Drafter specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Wenwei; he ranked third among his brothers and was aged twenty-three, born on the seventeenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather Shi and grandfather Chi were each posthumously granted the titles General of Cavalry and Assistant Commissioner-in-chief of the Chief Military Commission of the Rear Army. His father, Song, was Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Vice Commissioner-in-chief of the Chief Military Commission of the Rear Army. His father's former wives, née Zhang and née Fan, were each posthumously granted the title Lady; his mother was née Li. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother Bing was a military provincial graduate of the renchen year (1532) and a commander administering the Embroidered-uniform Guard. He married a woman née Liu. He placed one hundredth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and three hundred eighteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Jin was registered with the Jining Guard in Shandong and was a native of Laiyang Subprefecture [?]. He was a subprefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Shifu; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-five, born on the eighth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sheng, his grandfather Long, his father Xian, and his mother née Meng. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Qian, Zhou, and Yan [?—the division of these names is uncertain]. He married a woman née Xie. He placed sixty-fourth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and one hundred eighty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Zongmu, registered in a civilian household in Linhai County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an added-quota student of the prefectural school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Xinfu; he ranked second among his brothers and was aged twenty-two, born on the nineteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zuan; his grandfather was Yiqing, a medical official; his father was Xun; and his mother was née Zheng. He had grandparents and parents living. His elder brother was Zongyuan, and his younger brothers were Zongwei, Zongsi, Zongdan, and Zongluo. He married a woman née Qin. He placed third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and one hundred sixty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Xu Wentong 徐文通, courtesy name Rusi, was registered in an artisan household in Yongkang County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the National University, he specialized in the Book of Documents. He ranked eighty-eighth in family birth order and was aged thirty, born on the third day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Desheng; his grandfather, Ke; and his father, Shi, a county vice magistrate. His mother was née Sun. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Wenshu, and his wife was née Zhao. He placed twenty-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 212th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Feng Jin 馮覲, courtesy name Jinshu, was registered in an artisan household in Haining County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, and was a native of Qiantang County. A student of the National University, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He ranked first in family birth order and was aged thirty-six, born on the thirteenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Liang; his grandfather, Gui; and his father, Qian. His mother was née Chen. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Guan, Jian, Jue, Qin, Jing, Ji, and Kuan; his wife was née Bao. He placed twenty-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and twenty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Yichun 李宜春, courtesy name Yingyuan, was registered in a salt-producing household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian. A Confucian scholar, he specialized in the Book of Documents. He ranked second in family birth order and was aged thirty-three, born on the eighth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Mengjiao; his grandfather, Wan, a River Anchorage official; and his father, Yu. His mother was née Huang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Ren, and his younger brothers were Kaichun and Huichun; his wife was née Liu. He placed thirty-first in the Fujian Provincial Examination and thirty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huangfu Jin 皇甫溍, courtesy name Daolong, was registered in a civilian household in Changzhou County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the National University, he specialized in the Book of Changes. He ranked fourth in family birth order and was aged thirty-six, born on the eighth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tong; his grandfather, Xin, posthumously granted the title of Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites; and his father, Lu, a prefect, granted the title of Grand Master of Constitutional Rectitude. His mother, née Huang, had received successive grants of the title of Lady of Respect. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Chong, a tribute scholar; Xiao, an Assistant Surveillance Commissioner; and Fang, a bureau director in the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel. His wife was née Gu. He placed eighty-first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and second in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Xu Xueshi, registered in a military household in Shangyu County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an attached student of the county school and specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yiyan; he ranked eighteenth in his family, was aged twenty-eight, and was born on the fifteenth day of the intercalary twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Zheng; his grandfather was Fu, granted the cap and girdle of official status under provisions of imperial grace; his father was Zichen, a department magistrate; and his mother was née Ge. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brothers were Qiu, a school instructor, Xueshu, Xuedao, Xuexian, Xueli, Xueyi, Xueshu, Xuemeng, and Xueyan. (The two names rendered Xueshu are 學恕 and 學書.) He married a woman née Liu. He placed seventy-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Qiao, registered in an artisan household in Nanfeng County, Jianchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Wenji; he ranked first in his family, was aged thirty-three, and was born on the fourth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Kongrong, his grandfather was Qiong, his father was Luan, and his mother was née Shu. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Bai and Tan. He married a woman née Luo. He placed forty-seventh in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 165th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qian Jiayou, registered in an officer household of Zhenyuan Guard, Huguang, and a native of Zhenyuan Prefecture, Guizhou, was a student of the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Jingcheng; he ranked fourth in his family, was aged forty-five, and was born on the twenty-eighth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was An; his grandfather was Ning, General of Manifest Might; his father was Shan, granted the title General Who Cherishes the Distant; and his mother was née Xu, granted the title Lady of Chastity. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Jiaqing, Jiayan, and Jiamou. He married a woman née Zhou. He placed third in the Guizhou Provincial Examination and 296th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Wen, registered in a civilian household in Gui'an County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a county-school student and specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Rucheng; he ranked third in his family, was aged twenty-eight, and was born on the fifth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Zhen, a department magistrate; his grandfather was Song, a county magistrate; his father was Jie, a medical-school official; and his mother was née Chen. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Ji and Zhi. He married a woman née Pan. He placed seventy-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 155th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhao Yue, registered in a civilian household in Tongcheng County, Anqing Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Ziju; he ranked tenth in the family and was thirty-three years old, born on the twenty-ninth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xin, his grandfather Yongfang, his father Bi, and his mother née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Qin, an Official Attending Sacrifices; Rui, a tribute scholar (gongshi); Xi; and Jun. His younger brother was Zhu. He married a woman née Fang. He placed first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 108th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Ran, registered in a civilian household in Luanzhou, Yongping Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Ziyun; he ranked thirteenth in the family and was thirty-four years old, born on the first day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xian, his grandfather Tong, his father Zhen, and his mother née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Shangwen, Shangzhi, Shangjie, and Yihu [?]. He married a woman née Zhang and subsequently another woman née Zhang. He placed thirty-sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twenty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Zhong, registered in a civilian household in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was an attached student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Mingxiao; he ranked thirty-second in the family and was twenty-two years old, born on the eleventh day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rui; his grandfather Yuanchun was a Prefect, drew a third-rank salary, and had been advanced to the prestige title Grand Master of the Second Class (Yazhong dafu). His father was Deng and his mother née Li. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brothers were Shi, Zuo, Wei, Pei, and Hua. He married a woman née Zhao. He placed third in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 173rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wan Gong, registered in a military household in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Suqing; he ranked second in the family and was thirty years old, born on the twenty-third day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qinwu, his grandfather Mingda, his father Wenbing, and his mother née Hu. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brothers were Sicong and Sitai. He married a woman née Zhou. He placed twentieth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and ninety-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

林光祖〔貫廣東潮州府揭陽縣民籍，國子生，治書經，字以謙，行一，年三十七，八月二十七日生〕。曾祖鸞，祖愷，父文〔國子監學正〕，母陳氏，繼母鄭氏、楊氏。永感下，弟光裕，娶陳氏。廣東鄉試第三名，會試第六名。

張子弘〔貫江西吉安府廬陵縣軍籍，縣附學生，治詩經，字汝容，行十二，年三十三，三月初四日生〕。曾祖軾〔壽官〕，祖勵，父江〔知縣〕，母曾氏。慈侍下，兄子勲、子介，娶劉氏。江西鄉試第五十五名，會試第三十二名。
translation_en:
Tang Yu, registered in a civilian household in Haining County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Siping; he ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-eight years old, born on the ninth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was An; his grandfather, Lin, was an Assistant Instructor; his father, Shiqing, was an Assistant Prefect; and his mother was née Yang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Kui, and his younger brothers were Ji and Xie. His wife was née Yao. He placed sixteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu An, registered in a military household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Renfu; he ranked fourth among his brothers and was thirty-four years old, born on the first day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Li; his grandfather was Kai; his father, Xuan, was a Salt Transport Commissioner; and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Kuan, a student of the Directorate of Education, Bao, Ning, and Wan; his younger brother was Yin. His wife was née Xie. He placed forty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Guangzu, registered in a civilian household in Jieyang County, Chaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yiqian; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-seven years old, born on the twenty-seventh day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Luan; his grandfather was Kai; his father, Wen, was a School Corrector in the Directorate of Education; his mother was née Chen; and his stepmothers were née Zheng and née Yang. Both parents were deceased. His younger brother was Guangyu, and his wife was née Chen. He placed third in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Zihong, registered in a military household in Luling County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi, was an additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Rurong; he ranked twelfth among his brothers and was thirty-three years old, born on the fourth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather, Shi, held an honorary official title conferred for longevity; his grandfather was Li; his father, Jiang, was a District Magistrate; and his mother was née Zeng. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Zixun and Zijie, and his wife was née Liu. He placed fifty-fifth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and thirty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

舒春芳〔貫江西饒州府鄱陽縣民籍，縣學生，治易經，字景仁，行一，年二十七，十月初十日生〕。曾祖昱〔衛經歷〕，祖穆〔壽官〕，父載道〔終養進士〕，母程氏。具慶下，弟春和，娶劉氏。江西鄉試第三十八名，會試第二百四十一名。

劉佃〔貫江西吉安府廬陵縣民籍，安福縣人，府學附學生，治易經，字仲有，行三，年二十六，正月二十一日生〕。曾祖景隆〔遇例冠帶〕，祖梃〔遇例冠帶〕，父昉〔訓導〕，母王氏。重慶下，兄偲，弟倜、位，娶高氏。江西鄉試第八十六名，會試第一百二十八名。

張大中〔貫山東東昌府臨清州民籍，州學生，治書經，字子用，行一，年四十一，二月二十七日生〕。曾祖興，祖信，父功，母李氏，繼母趙氏。慈侍下，弟大才、大用、大業，娶王氏。山東鄉試第九名，會試第一百四十名。
translation_en:
Wang Xun, registered in an official household of the Chengdu Right Guard in Sichuan, was a National University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Keyong; he was first in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the twenty-fourth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yu, his grandfather Nan, and his father Zhe, a Guard Commander. His legal mother was née Ma and his birth mother née Liang. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Fang, and his wife was née Li. He placed fourth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and sixty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shu Chunfang, registered in a civilian household in Poyang County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Jingren; he was first in birth order, aged twenty-seven, and born on the tenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yu, a Guard Registrar; his grandfather was Mu, an honorary official by virtue of longevity; and his father was Zaidao, a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) on leave to care for an aged parent until the parent's death. His mother was née Cheng. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Chunhe, and his wife was née Liu. He placed thirty-eighth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 241st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Dian, registered in a civilian household in Luling County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi, and a native of Anfu County, was an attached student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zhongyou; he was third in birth order, aged twenty-six, and born on the twenty-first day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather Jinglong and grandfather Ting had each been granted the cap and girdle of official status under applicable regulations. His father was Fang, an Assistant Instructor, and his mother was née Wang. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brother was Si, his younger brothers were Ti and Wei, and his wife was née Gao. He placed eighty-sixth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 128th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Dazhong, registered in a civilian household in Linqing Subprefecture, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, was a subprefectural school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Ziyong; he was first in birth order, aged forty-one, and born on the twenty-seventh day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xing, his grandfather Xin, and his father Gong. His mother was née Li and his stepmother née Zhao. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His younger brothers were Dacai, Dayong, and Daye, and his wife was née Wang. He placed ninth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 140th in the Metropolitan Examination.

袁福徵〔貫直隸松江府華亭縣人，軍籍，府學生，治書經，字履善，行一，年二十四，七月三十日生〕。曾祖瑛〔知州〕，祖賁，父以嗣〔訓導〕，母唐氏。具慶下，兄元徵，弟嘉徵、孝徵、晉徵、夢徵，娶彭氏。應天府鄉試第九名，會試第一百十五名。
translation_en:
Deng Xiangrong 鄧向榮 was registered in a civilian household in Qingliu County, Tingzhou Prefecture, Fujian, and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Yuanzhi, he ranked first in birth order, and he was aged thirty-five, born on the twelfth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Deshi, his grandfather Wen, and his father Xuan, a County Vice Magistrate; his mother was née Wu, and both parents were living. His younger brothers were Xiangyong and Xiangdao, and his wife was née Tang. He placed sixteenth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and fifty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fang Jiuxu 方九敘 was registered in a civilian household in Qiantang County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Yuji, he ranked second in birth order, and he was aged thirty-eight, born on the thirteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhongren, his grandfather Gui, and his father apparently Ren; the maternal names are recorded as a former mother née Chai, a repeated née Chai, and mother née Chen [?]. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Jiugong, his younger brother Jiude, and his wife was née Jin. He placed twenty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 206th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tan Lun 譚綸 was registered in a military household in Yihuang County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, and was a Confucian scholar specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Zili, he ranked third in birth order, and he was aged twenty-five, born on the twenty-first day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ji, a student of the Directorate of Education, his grandfather Tingyong, and his father Gao, a Prefectural School Instructor; his father's former wife was née Huang and his mother née Luo, and both parents were living. His elder brother was Jing, his younger brother Fu, and his wife was née Rao. He placed eightieth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 204th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yuan Fuzheng 袁福徵 was a native of Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, registered in a military household, and a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Lüshan, he ranked first in birth order, and he was aged twenty-four, born on the thirtieth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ying, a Department Magistrate, his grandfather Ben, and his father Yisi, an Assistant Instructor; his mother was née Tang, and both parents were living. His elder brother was Yuanzheng, his younger brothers were Jiazheng, Xiaozheng, Jinzheng, and Mengzheng, and his wife was née Peng. He placed ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 115th in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:

周鍵〔貫四川叙州府富順縣，軍籍，縣學增廣生，治詩經，字啓夫，行八，年三十，正月初九日生〕。曾祖秉儒，祖萬斗〔贈戶部主事〕，父詔〔知府〕，前母彭氏〔贈安人〕，母方氏〔封安人〕。慈侍下，兄銳、鋕、錦〔引禮舍人〕、鋧、鈇、鉉、鍊，弟鐩、鈳、鎔，娶楊氏。四川鄉試第二十二名，會試第六十五名。

周爻〔貫四川叙州府宜賓縣，軍籍，國子生，治書經，字易夫，行二，年三十九，六月初八日生〕。曾祖友信，祖旋〔贈徵仕郎、義勇衛經歷〕，父嘉誥，母牟氏，繼母陳氏。具慶下，兄壬〔監生〕，弟令、典、冊、曆，娶吳氏，繼娶陳氏。四川鄉試第六名，會試第一百四十四名。

余文獻〔貫江西九江府德化縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字伯初，行一，年三十九，四月初五日生〕。曾祖旻，祖志琳，父仁，母王氏。嚴侍下，弟文華，娶陳氏。江西鄉試第三名，會試第六十二名。
translation_en:
Lu Mengbao, registered in Fengcheng County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a military household and was a student of the National University. He specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Wenwei; he ranked fourth among his brothers and was forty years old, born on the twentieth day of the second month. His great-grandfather, Juzai, had received an official commendation as a righteous commoner; his grandfather was Demei. His father, Shixu, was a government student, honorarily granted the titles of Gentleman of Scholarly Service and Prefectural Judge. His mother, née Du, was granted the title of Grand Dowager Gentlewoman. His mother alone survived. His elder brother Menglin was formerly an Investigating Censor. He married a woman née Wan, and subsequently women née Li and Jiang. He placed tenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 228th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Jian, registered in Fushun County, Xuzhou Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a military household and was an added-quota student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Qifu; he ranked eighth among his brothers and was thirty years old, born on the ninth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Bingru; his grandfather, Wandou, was posthumously granted the title of Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue. His father, Zhao, was a Prefect. His father's former wife, née Peng, was posthumously granted the title of Lady of Peace; his mother, née Fang, was granted the same title. His mother alone survived. His elder brothers were Rui, Zhi, Jin (a Court Usher), Xian, Fu, Xuan, and Lian; his younger brothers were Sui, Ke, and Rong. He married a woman née Yang. He placed twenty-second in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and sixty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Yao, registered in Yibin County, Xuzhou Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a military household and was a student of the National University. He specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yifu; he ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-nine years old, born on the eighth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Youxin; his grandfather, Xuan, was posthumously granted the titles of Gentleman for Attendant Service and Registry Manager of the Yiyong Guard. His father was Jiagao; his mother was née Mou, and his stepmother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brother Ren was a National University student; his younger brothers were Ling, Dian, Ce, and Li. He married a woman née Wu and subsequently a woman née Chen. He placed sixth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 144th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Wenxian, registered in Dehua County, Jiujiang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the National University. He specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Bochu; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-nine years old, born on the fifth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Min; his grandfather was Zhilin; his father was Ren, and his mother was née Wang. His father alone survived. His younger brother was Wenhua. He married a woman née Chen. He placed third in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and sixty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
項守禮〔貫浙江寧波府奉化縣，軍籍，縣學生，治詩經，字進伯，行一，年三十二，正月二十六日生〕。曾祖愫〔山西道監察御史〕，祖䫴〔府學訓導〕，父秀〔歲貢生〕，母周氏。嚴侍下，弟守義、守廉，娶沈氏。浙江鄉試第五十名，會試第三百一名。

王會〔貫直隸松江府華亭縣，匠籍，國子生，治易經，字子嘉，行一，年二十七，十二月十五日生〕。曾祖綸，祖瓚〔義官〕，父良玉，母杜氏。具慶下，兄章、命，弟俞、念、愈，娶陳氏。應天府鄉試第一百十九名，會試第三十八名。

蔣孝〔貫直隸常州府武進縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字惟忠，行二，年四十一，三月初四日生〕。曾祖賓，祖志，父瓛〔壽官〕，前母白氏，母馮氏。嚴侍下，兄節、堂、雲，娶華氏。應天府鄉試第三十一名，會試第二百十名。

陳士元〔貫湖廣德安府應城縣，軍籍，國子生，治易經，字心叔，行一，年二十九，三月十四日生〕。曾祖瑶，祖尚言〔散官〕，父正〔歲貢生〕，母華氏。具慶下，弟士充、士宅、士完、士光、士先，娶程氏。湖廣鄉試第十四名，會試第二十五名。
translation_en:
Xiang Shouli 項守禮 was registered in Fenghua County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a military household. A county government school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Jinbo and was first in birth order, aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-sixth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Su 愫, Investigating Censor for the Shanxi Circuit; his grandfather was Jin 䫴, an assistant instructor in a prefectural government school; his father was Xiu 秀, an annual tribute student; and his mother was née Zhou. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brothers were Shouyi and Shoulian, and his wife was née Shen. He ranked fiftieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 301st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Hui 王會 was registered in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered region, in an artisan household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Zijia and was first in birth order, aged twenty-seven, born on the fifteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lun 綸; his grandfather was Zan 瓚, an honorary official recognized for public benefaction; his father was Liangyu 良玉; and his mother was née Du. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zhang and Ming, his younger brothers were Yu 俞, Nian 念, and Yu 愈, and his wife was née Chen. He ranked 119th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jiang Xiao 蔣孝 was registered in Wujin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region, in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Weizhong and was second in birth order, aged forty-one, born on the fourth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bin 賓; his grandfather was Zhi 志; and his father was Huan 瓛, an honorary official recognized for longevity. His father's former wife was née Bai, and his mother was née Feng. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Jie, Tang, and Yun, and his wife was née Hua. He ranked thirty-first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 210th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Shiyuan 陳士元 was registered in Yingcheng County, De'an Prefecture, Huguang, in a military household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Xinshu and was first in birth order, aged twenty-nine, born on the fourteenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yao 瑶; his grandfather was Shangyan 尚言, an official with prestige rank; his father was Zheng 正, an annual tribute student; and his mother was née Hua. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Shichong, Shizhai, Shiwan, Shiguang, and Shixian, and his wife was née Cheng. He ranked fourteenth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and twenty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

鄔璉〔貫江西瑞州府新昌縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字宜瑩，行八，年三十二，四月二十一日生。〕曾祖三謨，祖尚縉，父承業，前母吳氏，母晏氏。慈侍下。兄璜，弟玘。娶胡氏。江西鄉試第七十八名，會試第二百四十九名。

計士元〔貫江西饒州府鄱陽縣，民籍，縣學生，治春秋，字允卿，行一，年二十九，七月初八日生。〕曾祖籌，祖尚賢，父仁〔散官〕，母羅氏。具慶下。弟士明、士竒、士良。娶江氏。江西鄉試第十四名，會試第一百五十六名。

陶欽臯〔貫江西九江府彭澤縣，民籍，縣學生，治禮記，字克允，行十四，年三十三，七月二十八日生。〕曾祖榮，祖焯〔醫學訓科〕，父埜〔醫學訓科，封文林郎、浙江道監察御史〕，母宋氏〔贈孺人〕，繼母劉氏。嚴侍下。兄欽民〔廩生〕、欽時、欽夔〔按察司副使〕、欽中〔監生〕。娶馮氏。江西鄉試第三名，會試第二百二十三名。
translation_en:
Chi Fengxiang, courtesy name Dezheng, was from Linqu County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, registered in a military household; a county government student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-nine, born on the twenty-second day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rang, a county vice magistrate; his grandfather was Yin; his father was Cong; and his mother, née Nie, was the surviving parent. His younger brother was Fengyi, and his wife was née Shen; he placed thirteenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 187th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Lian, courtesy name Yiying, was from Xinchang County, Ruizhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, registered in a civilian household; a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked eighth among his brothers and was aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-first day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sanmo; his grandfather was Shangjin; his father was Chengye; his father's former wife was née Wu; and his mother, née Yan, was the surviving parent. His elder brother was Huang and his younger brother was Qi; his wife was née Hu, and he placed seventy-eighth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 249th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ji Shiyuan, courtesy name Yunqing, was from Poyang County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, registered in a civilian household; a county government student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged twenty-nine, born on the eighth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chou; his grandfather was Shangxian; his father was Ren, a titular official; and his mother was née Luo, both parents being living. His younger brothers were Shiming, Shiqi, and Shiliang; his wife was née Jiang, and he placed fourteenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 156th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tao Qingao, courtesy name Keyun, was from Pengze County, Jiujiang Prefecture, Jiangxi, registered in a civilian household; a county government student specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked fourteenth among his brothers and was aged thirty-three, born on the twenty-eighth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rong; his grandfather was Chao, an instructor in the medical school; his father was Ye, an instructor in the medical school honorifically appointed Gentleman of Literary Service and investigating censor for the Zhejiang Circuit; his mother was née Song, posthumously granted the title Lady; and his stepmother was née Liu. His father was living; his elder brothers were Qinmin, a stipendiary government student, Qinshi, Qinkui, a vice surveillance commissioner, and Qinzhong, an Imperial University student. His wife was née Feng, and he placed third in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 223rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Liu Chaozuo, registered in a military household in Anfu County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Daoqing; he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-three, born on the nineteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zizan, his grandfather Rui, and his father Qian. His father’s former wife was née Wang, and his mother was née Wu. Both parents were living. His elder brother, Chaoyong, had been granted the cap and belt of official status under provisions of imperial grace; his younger brother was Chaojie. His wife was née Wang. He placed nineteenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and thirty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Shizhen, registered in a military household in Guantao County, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zichang; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged twenty-nine, born on the twentieth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sheng, his grandfather Jun, and his father Jie. His father’s former wife was née Wang, and his mother was née Wu. His mother alone was living. His wife was née Zong. He placed twelfth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 244th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Ermu, registered in a civilian household in Dongping Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, was an added-quota student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Chengqing; he ranked second among his brothers and was aged twenty, born on the eighth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather Hai was posthumously granted the titles of Vice Minister of War and Right Vice Censor-in-chief. His grandfather En was granted the title of Right Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review and posthumously granted the titles of Vice Minister of War and Right Vice Censor-in-chief. His father Yuanqing was Grand Master for Thorough Counsel, Vice Minister of War, and concurrently Right Vice Censor-in-chief of the Censorate. His mother, née Li, was granted the title Lady of Gentleness; his birth mother was née Zhang. His father alone was living. His elder brother Ergeng was a student admitted by virtue of his father’s official status; his younger brothers were Erzhuan and Erbu. His wife was née Zhao. He placed twenty-fifth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 243rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Daqi, registered in a civilian household in Nancheng County, Jianchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zichong; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-nine, born on the thirtieth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yizhong, his grandfather Zijing, and his father Hong, an Assistant Instructor. His mother was née Zou. Both parents were living. His wife was née Zuo, and his subsequent wife was née Shan. He placed fifty-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 125th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Xiong Ruda, registered in a military household in Jinxian County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was an additional student at the county school specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Deming, he ranked eighth among his brothers, and he was twenty-five, born on the second day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shumin, his grandfather Huaidao, and his father Yu; his mother was née Wan, and his stepmothers were née Wei and née Zhu. His grandparents and parents were living; his elder brother was Zhan, and his younger brothers were Yuqi [?], Wang, Yang, Ji, and Shu. He married a woman née Min and placed seventh in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 315th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Bi Qiang, registered in an artisan household in Shidai County, Chizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a county-school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Tingming, he ranked third among his brothers, and he was twenty-eight, born on the fifth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gengsheng, his grandfather Gui, and his father Yonggao; his father's former wife was née Wan, his mother was née Cui, and his stepmother was née Sun. Both parents were living; his elder brothers were Gang and Zhong. He married a woman née Shao and placed 104th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Yiju, registered in a civilian household in Chengdu County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Deqing, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was thirty-eight, born on the first day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yanzhao, his grandfather Qian, and his father Zuo; his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Gao and placed first in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and seventy-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fan Jie, registered in a military household in Jimo County, Jiaozhou Subprefecture, Laizhou Prefecture, Shandong, was an added-quota student at the county school specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Jingzhi, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was twenty-eight, born on the twenty-first day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qing, his grandfather Neng, and his father Peng; his father's former wife was née Wang, his stepmother was née Liu, and his birth mother was née Chen. His father was deceased and his mother living; his elder brother was Bi, and his younger brothers were Fang, Sheng, Qian, Mo, and Tao. He married a woman née Yang and placed eighteenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and eightieth in the Metropolitan Examination.
