吳朝鳳，貫浙江溫州府樂清縣，軍籍，國子生。治詩經，字鳴仲，行三十一，年四十，二月十四日生。曾祖綸〔通議大夫南京禮部右侍郎贈本部尚書謚恭毅〕，祖玄應〔正奉大夫廣東右布政使〕，父九仁，母金氏。嚴侍下，兄朝鈛、朝鍵，弟朝球、朝鈍、朝鸞、朝鵬、朝陞、朝並、朝寯、朝鉠，娶趙氏。浙江鄉試第二十一名，會試第一百七十五名。
translation_en:
Wang Yiyang was registered in Jiangdu County, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region (Zhili), in a military household, and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Zifu. He ranked first in birth order, was thirty-five years old, and was born on the twenty-second day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Jue [honorary official for longevity]; his grandfather was Fu [County Magistrate]; and his father was Qian [student of the Directorate of Education]. His mother was née Sun, and his stepmother was née Lin. His father was deceased and his mother was living. His younger brothers were Yide, Yiyan, Yikui, Yigong, Yizheng, Yicheng, Yi’en, Yiru, Yiju, Yizhen, Yifang, and Yizhi. He was betrothed to a woman née Wu and married a woman née Shen. He placed 114th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 105th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Zichong was registered in Ruyang County, Runing Prefecture, Henan, in a civilian household, and was a prefectural school student. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Zhongshi. He ranked second in birth order, was thirty-four years old, and was born on the eleventh day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Gong; his grandfather was Qin [honorary official for longevity]; and his father was Ze [County Magistrate]. His father’s former wife was née Yang, and his mother was née Fang. His father was deceased and his mother was living. His elder brother was Ziwan, and his younger brothers were Ziguan and Zimin. He married a woman née Pi and subsequently a woman née Wang. He placed thirty-seventh in the Henan Provincial Examination and 237th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Linyang was registered in Jiangjin County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, in a military household, and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Ruzhen. He ranked third in birth order, was thirty-eight years old, and was born on the sixth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Shu [honorary official for longevity]; his grandfather was Mengqi; and his father was Zhou. His mother was née Zhou. His father was living and his mother was deceased. His elder brothers were Fuyang and Zaiyang. He married a woman née Quan. He placed twenty-fourth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 233rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Chaofeng was registered in Yueqing County, Wenzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a military household, and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Mingzhong. He ranked thirty-first in birth order, was forty years old, and was born on the fourteenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Lun [Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Right Vice Minister of Rites at Nanjing, posthumously appointed Minister of Rites at Nanjing and given the posthumous name Gongyi]; his grandfather was Xuanying [Grand Master for Upright Service and Right Provincial Administration Commissioner of Guangdong]; and his father was Jiuren. His mother was née Jin. His father was living and his mother was deceased. His elder brothers were Chaoguo and Chaojian, and his younger brothers were Chaoqiu, Chaodun, Chaoluan, Chaopeng, Chaosheng, Chaobing, Chaojun, and Chaoyang. He married a woman née Zhao. He placed twenty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 175th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Kang Diji 康迪吉 was registered in Zhangqiu County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, in a military household. A county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Daofu and was second in birth order, aged twenty-six, born on the fourth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Le; his grandfather was Yue, an Office Manager; and his father was Jimin, a provincial sacrificial official (shengjiguan). His father's former wife was née Li, and his mother was née Hu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Xiuji, and his younger brother was Fengji. His wife was née Ning. He ranked fifty-sixth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and forty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Huai 陳淮 was registered in Fenghua County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household. A county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Yuzhi and was second in birth order, aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-eighth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhongsu, his grandfather was Yuan, and his father was Jin; his mother was née Yuan. His mother alone was living. His elder brother was Ze, and his younger brother was He. His wife was née Wu. He ranked eighty-sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 253rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

姜良翰〔貫浙江金華府金華縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字希召，行九，年三十六，十二月二十二日生〕。曾祖約〔吏部文選司主事，陞廣東南雄府知府〕，祖瑛〔知縣〕，父淮〔知縣〕，母嚴氏。具慶下，兄良輔〔大使〕、良能、良臣、良佐、良弼、良高、良相、良卿、良應，弟良豪、良采、良詒，娶陳氏。浙江鄉試第一名，會試第二百一十八名。

劉鳳〔貫直隸蘇州府長洲縣，民籍，府學生，治易經，字子威，行一，年二十八，六月二十九日生〕。曾祖镗，祖相〔義官〕，父梅〔推官〕，前母俞氏，母吳氏。具慶下，娶顧氏。應天府鄉試第七十一名，會試第二十九名。
translation_en:
Third class: 216 men, granted the status of equivalent metropolitan graduate (tong jinshi chushen).

Cao Sanyang, registered in Yixing County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a county government school student specializing in the Record of Rites. His courtesy name was Zitai; he ranked third in his family and was twenty-nine years old, born on the sixteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Li, his grandfather Zhao, and his father Pei; his mother was née Mao and his stepmother née Shi. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yiyang and Eryang; his younger brothers were Jingyang, Yingyang, Mingyang, Bingyang, and Chunyang. His wife was née Lü. He placed fifth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 141st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jiang Lianghan, registered in Jinhua County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Xizhao; he ranked ninth in his family and was thirty-six years old, born on the twenty-second day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather Yue was a Secretary in the Bureau of Personnel Appointments of the Ministry of Personnel, promoted to Prefect of Nanxiong Prefecture, Guangdong; his grandfather Ying and father Huai were County Magistrates. His mother was née Yan. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Liangfu, a Commissioner, Liangneng, Liangchen, Liangzuo, Liangbi, Lianggao, Liangxiang, Liangqing, and Liangying; his younger brothers were Lianghao, Liangcai, and Liangyi. His wife was née Chen. He placed first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 218th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Feng, registered in Changzhou County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a prefectural government school student specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Ziwei; he ranked first in his family and was twenty-eight years old, born on the twenty-ninth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tang, his grandfather Xiang held the title of Official for Righteousness, and his father Mei was a Prefectural Judge. His father's former wife was née Yu, and his mother was née Wu. Both parents were living. His wife was née Gu. He placed seventy-first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twenty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

陳其學〔貫山東登州衛，軍籍，直隸宣城縣人，登州府學生，治《禮記》，字宗孟，行三，年三十三，二月二十四日生〕。曾祖安〔七品散官〕，祖善〔贈禮科給事中〕，父昪〔應天府府尹〕，前母王氏，母王氏，繼母王氏。慈侍下，兄邦治、邦禮、其可、其愚〔監生〕，弟其立、其居，娶王氏。山東鄉試第三名，會試第一百二十九名。

吉來獻〔貫陝西西安府興平縣，民籍，國子生，治《春秋》，字子欽，行二，年三十四，七月初七日生〕。曾祖贇，祖友文，父體仁〔貢士〕，母劉氏。慈侍下，兄來逢，弟來朝、來旬、來宣，娶王氏。陝西鄉試第五名，會試第二百五十四名。

translation_en:
Shen Jie 申价, courtesy name Maode, was registered in a civilian household in Yongnian County, Guangping Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked second in family order and was twenty-nine sui, born on the second day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather Guang was a Registrar, posthumously granted the title of Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel; his grandfather Lun was a Surveillance Vice Commissioner; and his father Han was a Subprefectural Judge. His mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Shi; his younger brothers were Wei, a tribute student, Chu, Bei, Zhuo, Qiao, and Yan. His wife was née Zhang. He placed forty-third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 290th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Qixue 陳其學, courtesy name Zongmeng, was registered in a military household of Dengzhou Guard, Shandong, and was a native of Xuancheng County in the directly administered metropolitan region. A Dengzhou prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked third in family order and was thirty-three sui, born on the twenty-fourth day of the second month. His great-grandfather An held a seventh-rank prestige title; his grandfather Shan was posthumously granted the title of Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Rites; and his father Bian was Prefect of Yingtian. His father's former wife, his mother, and his stepmother were all née Wang. His mother alone was living. His elder brothers were Bangzhi, Bangli, Qike, and Qiyu, an Imperial University student; his younger brothers were Qili and Qiju. His wife was née Wang. He placed third in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 129th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ji Laixian 吉來獻, courtesy name Ziqin, was registered in a civilian household in Xingping County, Xi'an Prefecture, Shaanxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked second in family order and was thirty-four sui, born on the seventh day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Yun; his grandfather was Youwen; and his father was Tiren, a tribute student. His mother was née Liu. His mother alone was living. His elder brother was Laifeng; his younger brothers were Laichao, Laixun, and Laixuan. His wife was née Wang. He placed fifth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 254th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Xi 章熙, courtesy name Yaozai, was registered in a civilian household in Haiyang County, Chaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked second in family order and was thirty-nine sui, born on the eleventh day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Fan; his grandfather was Kai; and his father was Tingxiu. His father's former wife was née Yao, and his mother was née Zhu. His father alone was living. His elder brother Huan was a Prefectural Vice Prefect; his younger brothers were Ye and Bing. His wife was née Fu. He placed fourth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 265th in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
馬錫〔貫河南開封府祥符縣軍籍，國子生，治易經，字伯厚，行三，年三十五，十一月初五日生〕。曾祖三，祖通，父文奎，母常氏。具慶下，兄鏜、鑑，弟鈿、銶、鍇，娶髙氏。河南鄉試第四十六名，會試第一百九十一名。

張承憲〔貫直隸松江府華亭縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字監先，行二，年二十六，三月十一日生〕。曾祖瑄〔贈監察御史〕，祖紳，父應祥，母胡氏。具慶下，兄宇、承宗，弟宿、承祖〔監生〕、承學、承守、承甫，娶楊氏。應天府鄉試第八名，會試第二十六名。

趙世奎〔貫神武右衛右所軍籍，直隸江都縣人，國子生，治詩經，字啓文，行八，年三十九，七月二十日生〕。曾祖旺，祖演〔贈文林郎、雲南道監察御史〕，父琪〔義官〕，母張氏，繼母王氏。永感下，兄世瞻、世普〔歲貢生〕、世顯、世煥、世卿，娶姬氏。順天府鄉試第三十一名，會試第一百二十七名。

葉材〔貫錦衣衛校尉籍，直隸常州府武進縣人，國子生，治詩經，字達卿，行六，年四十三，正月二十六日生〕。曾祖榮，祖元亨，父英〔封知縣〕，母潘氏〔贈孺人〕，繼母朱氏。慈侍下，兄林〔知縣〕、彬、松、桓、權，弟相，娶曹氏，繼娶吳氏。應天府鄉試第三十七名，會試第一百六十一名。
translation_en:
Ma Xi 馬錫, registered in a military household in Xiangfu County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Bohou, he ranked third among his brothers, and he was thirty-five years old, born on the fifth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was San, his grandfather Tong, his father Wenkui, and his mother née Chang; both parents were living. His elder brothers were Tang and Jian, and his younger brothers Dian, Qiu, and Kai; his wife was née Gao. He placed forty-sixth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 191st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Chengxian 張承憲, registered in a civilian household in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Jianxian, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was twenty-six years old, born on the eleventh day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xuan (posthumously appointed Investigating Censor), his grandfather Shen, his father Yingxiang, and his mother née Hu; both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yu and Chengzong, and his younger brothers Su, Chengzu (a student of the Directorate of Education), Chengxue, Chengshou, and Chengfu; his wife was née Yang. He placed eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twenty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Shikui 趙世奎, registered in a military household of the Right Battalion of the Shenwu Right Guard and originally from Jiangdu County in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Qiwen, he ranked eighth among his brothers, and he was thirty-nine years old, born on the twentieth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wang, his grandfather Yan (posthumously granted the rank of Gentleman for Attending the Forest of Literature and appointed Investigating Censor for the Yunnan Circuit), his father Qi (an honorary official for public benefaction), his mother née Zhang, and his stepmother née Wang; both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Shizhan, Shipu (an annual tribute student), Shixian, Shihuan, and Shiqing; his wife was née Ji. He placed thirty-first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 127th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ye Cai 葉材, registered in a household of a commandant of the Embroidered-Uniform Guard and originally from Wujin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Daqing, he ranked sixth among his brothers, and he was forty-three years old, born on the twenty-sixth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rong, his grandfather Yuanheng, his father Ying (honorarily appointed District Magistrate), his mother née Pan (posthumously granted the title Lady), and his stepmother née Zhu; his father was deceased, and he served his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Lin (District Magistrate), Bin, Song, Huan, and Quan, and his younger brother was Xiang; he married a woman née Cao and subsequently a woman née Wu. He placed thirty-seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 161st in the Metropolitan Examination.

任璜〔貫陝西西安府臨潼縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字北玉，行五，年三十八，九月十二日生〕。曾祖信，祖昶，父動陽，母賈氏。慈侍下，兄珮、玠、環、珠、珪、璣、瑤，弟瑱，娶鄧氏。陝西鄉試第三十一名，會試第一百七十名。

文方〔貫四川重慶府合州民籍，州學增廣生，治易經，字子靜，行五，年二十七，三月初七日生〕。曾祖仲清，祖獻，父誠〔知州〕，母劉氏。慈侍下，兄伯鈞、斗、璧、言、鑒、衡、啓，娶王氏，繼娶王氏。四川鄉試第七名，會試第二十二名。

translation_en:
Huo Ji, registered in a military household in Xiaoyi County, Fenzhou, Shanxi, was a county school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Yaofeng; he ranked first in birth order and was twenty-nine years old, born on the twenty-ninth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shen, his grandfather Feng, and his father Wen; his mother was née Guo. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed ninth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 186th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ren Huang, registered in a civilian household in Lintong County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, was a National University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Beiyu; he ranked fifth in birth order and was thirty-eight years old, born on the twelfth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xin, his grandfather Chang, and his father Dongyang; his mother was née Jia. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Pei, Jie, Huan, Zhu, Gui, Ji, and Yao; his younger brother was Tian. He married a woman née Deng. He placed thirty-first in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 170th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wen Fang, registered in a civilian household in Hezhou, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, was an added-quota student at the department school, specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Zijing; he ranked fifth in birth order and was twenty-seven years old, born on the seventh day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhongqing, his grandfather Xian, and his father Cheng, a department magistrate; his mother was née Liu. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Bojun [?], Dou, Bi, Yan, Jian, Heng, and Qi. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently another woman née Wang. He placed seventh in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and twenty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Dexi, registered in a military salt-producing household in Fuqing County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was an attached student at the county school, specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Zongru; he ranked first in birth order and was twenty-nine years old, born on the twenty-seventh day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jun, his grandfather Jun, and his father Wencai; his mother was née Fang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Deye and Dechang; his younger brothers were Dewei and Dexun. He married a woman née Zheng. He placed sixty-fourth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 205th in the Metropolitan Examination.

陳絳〔貫浙江紹興府上虞縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字用陽，行十九，年三十二，五月十五日生〕。曾祖太滂，祖頊，父述，母俞氏，繼母吳氏。具慶下，兄繪〔歲貢生〕、緒〔同科進士〕、紹〔知府〕、級、緩，弟綰，娶丁氏。浙江鄉試第六十一名，會試第四十三名。
translation_en:
Huang Guoqing, a student of the Imperial University, was registered in a civilian household in Jieyang County, Chaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Junren, and he ranked fifteenth in family birth order. He was thirty-four, born on the third day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chong, his grandfather Sancai, his father Bangjie, and his mother née Zhang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Guobao and his younger brother Guozhi; he married a woman née Zhang. He placed sixtieth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and thirty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shang Xun, a student of the Imperial University, was registered in a military household in Wugong County, Qian Subprefecture, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Dexin, and he ranked first in family birth order. He was forty-two, born on the sixth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhong, his grandfather Lian, and his father Da, a Police Chief. His father’s former wife was née Dang, and his mother was née Jia. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Lan, Vice Commissioner of the Institute of Imperial Handicrafts, Wan, and Yun; his younger brothers were Fang, a tribute scholar (gongshi), Tingchen, Tingxi, and Tingxiang. He married a woman née Ma. He placed fifty-fifth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and three hundred second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Tan, a student of the Imperial University, was registered in a civilian household in Ji County, Weihui Prefecture, Henan. He specialized in the Record of Rites; his courtesy name was Zijian, and he ranked fourth in family birth order. He was thirty-eight, born on the fourth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shisan, his grandfather Shun, his father Jinghe, and his mother née Kang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Mei, Ju, and Nan; he married a woman née Zhang. He placed fifth in the Henan Provincial Examination and three hundred seventeenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Jiang, a student of the Imperial University, was registered in a civilian household in Shangyu County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Yongyang, and he ranked nineteenth in family birth order. He was thirty-two, born on the fifteenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Taipang, his grandfather Xu, his father Shu, his mother née Yu, and his stepmother née Wu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Hui, an annual tribute student; Xu, a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the same examination year; Shao, a Prefect; Ji; and Huan. His younger brother was Wan. He married a woman née Ding. He placed sixty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and forty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
蔣賁〔貫廣西桂林府全州民籍，國子生，治易經，字子素，行四，年三十一，十月初九日生〕。曾祖鏠，祖基，父曉，母唐氏。慈侍下，兄賢〔省祭官〕、員，娶陶氏。廣西鄉試第二十八名，會試第三百三名。

王民〔貫山東東昌府臨清州民籍，州學生，治詩經，字皞如，行一，年三十四，十一月初七日生〕。曾祖王，祖和，父琮，母薛氏。慈侍下，娶張氏。山東鄉試第三十六名，會試第二百一名。

朱熙載〔貫山東平山衛旗籍，直隸揚州府太興縣人，國子生，治易經，字懋勳，行一，年三十一，十月初三日生〕。曾祖宏〔誥封奉直大夫戶部員外郎〕，祖榮〔苑馬寺少卿〕，父堂〔主簿〕，母王氏。具慶下，娶陳氏。山東鄉試第四十三名，會試第二百七十四名。

徐易〔貫江西廣信府永豐縣民籍，府學附學生，治書經，字希文，行六十八，年二十八，十二月十八日生〕。曾祖茂仙，祖紀，父瓊，母周氏。嚴侍下，兄昊、晟，娶全氏。江西鄉試第九十五名，會試第一百九十七名。
translation_en:
Jiang Ben 蔣賁, courtesy name Zisu, was registered in a civilian household in Quanzhou, Guilin Prefecture, Guangxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked fourth among his brothers and male cousins, was thirty-one sui, and was born on the ninth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Feng; his grandfather, Ji; his father, Xiao; and his mother, née Tang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Xian, a sacrificial official (shengjiguan), and Yuan. He married a woman née Tao. He placed twenty-eighth in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and 303rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Min 王民, courtesy name Haoru, was registered in a civilian household in Linqing Subprefecture, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong. A subprefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first among his brothers and male cousins, was thirty-four sui, and was born on the seventh day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wang; his grandfather, He; his father, Cong; and his mother, née Xue. His mother was living and his father deceased. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed thirty-sixth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 201st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Xizai 朱熙載, courtesy name Maoxun, was registered in a military banner household of Pingshan Guard, Shandong, and was a native of Taixing County [太興; ?], Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first among his brothers and male cousins, was thirty-one sui, and was born on the third day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather Hong had been granted by imperial patent the titles of Grand Master for Upright Service and Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue. His grandfather Rong was Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Herds; his father Tang was a Registrar; and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Chen. He placed forty-third in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 274th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Yi 徐易, courtesy name Xiwen, was registered in a civilian household in Yongfeng County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi. An attached student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked sixty-eighth among his brothers and male cousins, was twenty-eight sui, and was born on the eighteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Maoxian; his grandfather, Ji; his father, Qiong; and his mother, née Zhou. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Hao and Sheng. He married a woman née Quan. He placed ninety-fifth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 197th in the Metropolitan Examination.

俞介〔貫浙江紹興府餘姚縣匠籍，國子生，治易經，字仲和，行一，年三十八，十月十七日生〕。曾祖固禎〔壽官〕，祖欽，父瀾〔知縣〕，母徐氏。慈侍下，弟仝，娶韓氏，繼娶姜氏。浙江鄉試第四十名，會試第十一名。

錢嶧〔貫浙江寧波府鄞縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字景魯，行六十，年三十二，正月十九日生〕。曾祖秬〔縣丞，贈太中大夫、資治少尹、左參政〕，祖奐〔正奉大夫、正治卿、左布政使〕，父瓚〔中憲大夫、按察司副使〕，嫡母毛氏、李氏，生母王氏。永感下，兄崐〔知縣〕、峰、岑〔歲貢生〕、嵠、崡，弟岝，娶周氏，繼娶王氏。浙江鄉試第八名，會試第九十六名。

金九成〔貫直隸常州府武進縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字鳴韶，行二，年三十五，十月二十九日生〕。曾祖洪，祖俊，父珮，母楊氏。具慶下，兄昇、星、九齡〔同科進士〕，弟九皐、九思，娶陳氏。應天府鄉試第四十九名，會試第二百四十九名。
translation_en:
Xiang Hongmai, registered in a civilian household in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a county school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Jinggao; he ranked twenty-first in his family and was thirty-seven years old, born on the seventh day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bingzhi, a School Instructor; his grandfather was Tang; his father was Jin; and his mother was née Qiu. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Hongyi, Hongshi, and Hongxin, and his younger brother was Shang. He married a woman née Lu. He placed seventy-eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fifty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Jie, registered in an artisan household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Zhonghe; he ranked first in his family and was thirty-eight years old, born on the seventeenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Guzhen, an honorary official recognized for longevity; his grandfather was Qin; his father was Lan, a District Magistrate; and his mother was née Xu. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brother was Tong. He married a woman née Han and subsequently a woman née Jiang. He placed fortieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and eleventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qian Yi, registered in a civilian household in Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Jinglu; he ranked sixtieth in his family and was thirty-two years old, born on the nineteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ju, a District Vice Magistrate, posthumously granted the titles Grand Master of Palace Leisure (Taizhong dafu), Junior Aide for Governance (Zizhi shaoyin), and Administration Vice Commissioner of the Left. His grandfather was Huan, who held the titles Grand Master for Proper Service (Zhengfeng dafu), Minister for Proper Governance (Zhengzhi qing), and Provincial Administration Commissioner of the Left. His father was Zan, Grand Master for Constitutional Rectitude (Zhongxian dafu) and Surveillance Vice Commissioner. His legal mothers were née Mao and née Li; his birth mother was née Wang. His parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Kun, a District Magistrate; Feng; Cen, an annual tribute student; Xi; and Han. His younger brother was Zuo. He married a woman née Zhou and subsequently a woman née Wang. He placed eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and ninety-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jin Jiucheng, registered in a civilian household in Wujin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Mingshao; he ranked second in his family and was thirty-five years old, born on the twenty-ninth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hong; his grandfather was Jun; his father was Pei; and his mother was née Yang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Sheng, Xing, and Jiuling, the last a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the same examination year. His younger brothers were Jiugao and Jiusi. He married a woman née Chen. He placed forty-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 249th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Hong Yu, registered in a civilian household in Licheng County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, was a prefectural government student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Boshi; he ranked third among his brothers and was aged thirty-seven, born on the fourth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Tan; his grandfather Xiu and father Huai both held the honorary designation of Official for Righteousness. His father's principal wife was née Zhang, and his birth mother was née Mi. His father alone was still living. His elder brothers were Jin and Rao, and his younger brother was Sui. He married née Liu and subsequently née Wang. He placed twentieth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 284th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ren Huan, registered in an artisan household in Changzhi County, Lu'an Prefecture, Shanxi, was an additional student at the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Yingqian; he ranked second among his brothers and was aged twenty-six, born on the eighteenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Zeng, his grandfather Shineng, and his father Ao. His father's principal wife was née Zhang, and his birth mother was née Zhao. Both parents were still living. His elder brother Qi was a medical officer. He married née Li. He placed sixty-first in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 271st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Shilu, registered in a military household in Fenzhou, Shanxi, was an additional student at the subprefectural school specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Rugong; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-seven, born on the second day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Xing, his grandfather Fu, his father Tingbi, and his mother née Liu. His father alone was still living. His younger brother was Shichen. He married née Ren. He placed forty-first in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 242nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ouyang Zhen, registered in a civilian household in Ba County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, and originally from Taihe County, Jiangxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Qishu; he ranked second among his brothers and was aged forty-four, born on the eighth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Long, his grandfather Zhongqian, and his father Run. His father's former wife was née Zhang, and his mother was née Du. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother Fu was a tribute scholar (gongshi). He married née Hang. He placed thirty-seventh in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 307th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yan Dong 閻東, registered in a civilian household in Neijiang County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Qiming; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-nine, born on the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chengqing, his grandfather Zongqi, and his father Guang; his mother was née Wang. His mother alone was still living. His younger brothers were Yuan, Heng, Ren, and Yong [?]. He married a woman née Pan and subsequently a woman née Ma. He placed fifty-fourth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 206th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Qiyi 盧岐嶷, registered in a military household in Changtai County, Zhangzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Xiji; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty, born on the twelfth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Weizhen, his grandfather Deji, and his father Daoming; his mother was née Xue. His father alone was still living. He married a woman née Dai. He placed eighth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and thirty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tang Shouxun 唐守勲, registered in a civilian household in Panyu County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yunmao; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-four, born on the twenty-eighth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Guangji, his grandfather Jinghua, and his father Jiong; his mother was née Tan. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Shouming, Shouwen, Shoumo, and Shoujing. He married a woman née Wang. He placed fourteenth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and forty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Zhao 孫昭, registered in a civilian household in Yongjia County, Wenzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Mingde; he ranked second among his brothers and was aged twenty-seven, born on the thirteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yi, his grandfather Pao, and his father Cang. His father's former wives were née Ding and née Chen; his mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Yao and his younger brother Zui. He married a woman née Chen. He placed seventy-sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and sixty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Bengu, registered in Xingtai County, Shunde Prefecture, in the Metropolitan Region, belonged to a military household and was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zimin; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-one, born on the tenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xin, his grandfather Ying, and his father Zhao. His father's former wife was née Zhang, and his mother was née Chen. His mother alone was still living. He married a woman née Cao and subsequently a woman née Liu. He placed thirty-fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 298th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ni Run, registered in Dahe Guard in the Metropolitan Region, belonged to a military household and was originally from Changshu County, Suzhou Prefecture. He was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Boyu; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged forty-four, born on the twelfth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Neng, his grandfather Yu, his father He, and his mother née Yang. His father alone was still living. His younger brother was Lan, and he married a woman née Zhang. He placed twenty-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 258th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Shixin, registered in Xinchang County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Bojun; he ranked twenty-third among his brothers and was aged twenty-nine, born on the thirteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather Duo was Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Huguang, posthumously granted the titles of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Right Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate. His grandfather Pu was posthumously granted the title of Investigating Censor; his father Rou was a Prefectural Judge, and his mother was née Pan. Both parents were still living. His younger brothers were Shifang and Shiruo, and he married a woman née Dong. He placed seventy-eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 299th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qiu Bingwen, registered in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a military household and was a National University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Mingzhou; he ranked third among his brothers and was aged thirty-two, born on the second day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather Shan was a Surveillance Vice Commissioner; his grandfather Shouyuan held the honorary designation of Official for Righteousness; his father Maotang was a tribute scholar (gongshi). His mother was née Chen, and his stepmother was née Lin. Both parents were still living. His elder brother was Ling (Binghe), and his younger brothers were Jie, Sheng, Yu, Dongcheng, Bingxing, Bingxuan, Donglu, and Dongzhou. He married a woman née Chen and subsequently a woman née Hong. He placed fifty-first in the Fujian Provincial Examination and forty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Hu 王斛 was registered in Hanyang County, Hanyang Prefecture, Huguang, in a civilian household. A prefectural government student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Yingwan and ranked second among his brothers; he was twenty years old and was born on the twenty-ninth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jizong; his grandfather, Qing; and his father, Jiao, a Registrar in a guard. His mother was née Wu, and his stepmother was née Tao. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Jiao 角, and his younger brothers were Xie 觧, Cheng 頳, Quan 觠, and Shang 觴. He married a woman née Zhu. He placed twenty-sixth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 182nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Miao Xuan 繆宣 was registered in Changshu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region, in a civilian household, and was a native of Wu County. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Shihua and ranked fourth among his brothers; he was forty-one years old and was born on the first day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shishi; his grandfather, Gao, held an honorary rank for longevity; his father was Jing, and his mother was née Chen. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Yin, Chen, and Shi, and his younger brothers were Cai, Chong, Shou, and Wan. He married a woman née Li. He placed seventy-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 122nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Guangzu 王光祖 was registered in Wei County, Daming Prefecture, in the directly administered region, in a civilian household, and was a native of Licheng County, Shanxi. A county government student specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Zixiao and ranked first among his brothers; he was twenty-seven years old and was born on the seventh day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qi; his grandfather, Wen; his father, Jiong; and his mother, née Shen. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Guangkao. He married a woman née Ma. He placed fourteenth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 117th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Song Guohua 宋國華 was registered in Fengxin County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, in a civilian household. Following two illegible characters [?], the entry identifies him as an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Chongle, and he ranked fifth among his brothers; he was thirty-four years old and was born on the fourth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Diji; his grandfather, Yue; his father, Qing, a tribute student; and his mother, née Xu. Both parents were deceased. His younger brother was Guoying. He married a woman née Huang. He placed twenty-sixth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and ninety-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Hu Ru’an, courtesy name Gongfu, was registered in Sanyuan County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-five, born on the twenty-seventh day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shan, his grandfather Ao, and his father Yanzhao; his mother was née Li, and his stepmothers were née Suo and née Yuan. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Runing, and his younger brothers were Rukuan and Ruhong. His wife was née Wang. He placed twenty-first in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 229th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Shijin, courtesy name Ziheng, was registered in Zhongmou County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, in a civilian household. A county school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged twenty-three, born on the fifth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Can, his grandfather Huan, and his father Chaoyang; his mother was née Hu. Both parents were living. His wife was née Guo. He placed thirty-fourth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 257th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Jingrong, courtesy name Ziren, was registered in Jiangdu County, Yangzhou Prefecture, Zhili, in a civilian household. A military student of the capital guards specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged forty-four, born on the twenty-eighth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhida, his grandfather Hai, and his father Ning; his mother was née Jia. His father was deceased, and he attended his living mother. His younger brothers were Jinghua, Jingfu, and Jinggui. His wife was née Zhang. He placed fourteenth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventy-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Cai, courtesy name Maocan, was registered in an official household of the Xi’an Rear Guard, Shaanxi, and was originally from Jiangdu County, Zhili. A Xi’an prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-nine, born on the eighth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather, 𥟵 [reading uncertain], was General of Conspicuous Valor and Guard Commander, posthumously granted the title of Assistant Regional Military Commissioner. His grandfather Sheng was Assistant Guard Commander, posthumously granted the titles of General of Conspicuous Valor and Assistant Regional Military Commissioner. His father Pengxiao was General of Conspicuous Valor and Assistant Regional Military Commissioner in the Shaanxi Regional Military Commission. His mother, née Hu, was invested as Lady of Respect and posthumously granted the title Lady of Virtue; his stepmother was née Yan, and his birth mother was née Mao. His father was deceased, and he attended his living mother. He married a woman née Yang, and subsequently women née Han and née Tang. He placed sixteenth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 128th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Chengxu, courtesy name Huaide, was registered in a civilian household in Gu’an County, Shuntian Prefecture. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Documents, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Zhen, a County Vice Magistrate; his grandfather was Duo; and his father was Cai, a Commissioner. His father’s former wife was Lady Gao, and his mother was Lady Hou. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Cheng’en and his younger brother Chengzuo; he married Lady Xin. He ranked twenty-third in the Shuntian Prefectural Provincial Examination and seventy-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Lu, courtesy name Weixue, was registered in a military household in Zhangqiu County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the third day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Xiong, his grandfather Le, his father Zongliang, and his mother Lady Yin. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Fu and his younger brothers Zhi and Zuo; he married Lady Miao. He ranked seventy-fifth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 283rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Zhixue, courtesy name Shuxing, was registered in a civilian household in Changshou County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged forty-three, and born on the eighth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was He, his grandfather Fan, and his father Yu; his legal mother was Lady Fang and his birth mother Lady Wang. Both parents were deceased. He married Lady Zhou. He ranked twenty-ninth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 130th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guo Weifan, courtesy name Jiefu, was registered in a civilian household in Jieyang County, Chaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged forty-three, and born on the fifth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Hongyi, his grandfather Jun, and his father Chun. His father’s former wife was Lady Chen, and his mother was Lady Du. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His elder brother was Shichen and his younger brother Weihan; he married Lady Yang. He ranked seventeenth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and thirty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

治易經字子初行一年三十十二月初二日生
曾祖祥〔知州〕　祖英　父汶　母顧氏

punctuated:
王楠〔貫直隸德州左衛軍籍，山東文登縣人，國子生，治易經，字子梁，行二，年四十，十二月二十七日生〕。曾祖福榮，祖聚〔壽官〕，父崇，母李氏。永感下，兄松，娶熊氏。山東鄉試第四名，會試第二百十九名。

王鳴臣〔貫江西吉安府泰和縣民籍，縣學附學生，治詩經，字汝文，行三，年三十一，六月初一日生〕。曾祖大溪〔壽官〕，祖學漁，父國賜，母顏氏。具慶下，兄舉臣、彥臣，弟哲臣、禮臣、元臣，娶蕭氏。江西鄉試第六十九名，會試第二百七十五名。

戚慎〔貫直隸寧國府宣城縣民籍，國子生，治易經，字汝初，行四，年三十五，十月初四日生〕。曾祖榮，祖琡，父亨，母胡氏。具慶下，兄悅、懌、忻，弟恬、惺、悌、忭、懷、恢，娶丁氏。應天府鄉試第一百十二名，會試第一百五十九名。

蔡朴〔貫直隸河間府滄州竈籍，州學生，治易經，字子初，行一，年三十，十二月初二日生〕。曾祖祥〔知州〕，祖英，父汶，母顧氏。具慶下，兄恭，弟栻，娶王氏。順天府鄉試第一百十五名，會試第一百二十三名。
translation_en:
Wang Nan, registered in a military household of the Dezhou Left Guard in Zhili and a native of Wendeng County, Shandong, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Ziliang, he ranked second in birth order, and he was aged forty, born on the twenty-seventh day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Furong, his grandfather Ju held an honorary longevity title, his father was Chong, and his mother was née Li; both parents were deceased, his elder brother was Song, his wife was née Xiong, and he placed fourth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 219th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Mingchen, registered in a civilian household in Taihe County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, was an attached student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Book of Poetry; his courtesy name was Ruwen, he ranked third in birth order, and he was aged thirty-one, born on the first day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather Daxi held an honorary longevity title, his grandfather was Xueyu, his father was Guoci, and his mother was née Yan; both parents were living, his elder brothers were Juchen and Yanchen, his younger brothers were Zhechen, Lichen, and Yuanchen, his wife was née Xiao, and he placed sixty-ninth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 275th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qi Shen, registered in a civilian household in Xuancheng County, Ningguo Prefecture, Zhili, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Ruchu, he ranked fourth in birth order, and he was aged thirty-five, born on the fourth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Rong, his grandfather Chu, his father Heng, and his mother née Hu; both parents were living, his elder brothers were Yue, Yi, and Xin, his younger brothers were Tian, Xing, Ti, Bian, Huai, and Hui, his wife was née Ding, and he placed 112th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 159th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cai Pu, registered in a salt-producing household in Cangzhou, Hejian Prefecture, Zhili, was a student of the departmental Confucian school specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Zichu, he ranked first in birth order, and he was aged thirty, born on the second day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather Xiang was a department magistrate, his grandfather was Ying, his father Wen, and his mother née Gu; both parents were living, his elder brother was Gong, his younger brother Shi, his wife was née Wang, and he placed 115th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 123rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

陳大賓〔貫湖廣荊州府江陵縣匠籍，府學生，治易經，字敬夫，行一，年二十九，六月初三日生〕。曾祖溥，祖伯泰，父琳，母趙氏，繼母卓氏。重慶下，娶艾氏，繼娶趙氏。山東鄉試第六十二名，會試第二百四十七名。

趙錦〔貫浙江紹興府餘姚縣竈籍，縣學生，治易經，字元朴，行五十，年二十九，二月初十日生〕。曾祖玟，祖昺〔贈刑部貴州司主事〕，父塤〔府同知〕，母諸氏〔贈安人〕，繼母魯氏〔封安人〕。具慶下，兄世美〔醫官〕、鎭、釡、鏵，弟鎔、鎮、鍊、金，娶尹氏。浙江鄉試第七十九名，會試第一百四十九名。

朱繪〔貫山西平定州守禦千戶所官籍，直隸鳳陽府懷遠縣人，治書經，字白甫，行八，年二十四，七月二十九日生〕。曾祖璽，祖鳳〔贈文林郎推官〕，父方〔右僉都御史〕，母董氏〔封孺人〕。具慶下，兄紀、紳、紱、綬、綵、綾，弟維、約，娶閻氏。山西鄉試第八名，會試第一百三十一名。

吉澄〔貫直隸大名府開州匠籍，國子生，治書經，字靜甫，行二，年三十八，六月十三日生〕。曾祖宣，祖倫，父陳〔長史〕，母劉氏。具慶下，兄薦，弟肅、慎、芳、禎、沾、芬、洽、沖、浩，娶段氏，繼娶李氏。順天府鄉試第八十五名，會試第一百七十八名。
translation_en:
Chen Dabin, registered in an artisan household in Jiangling County, Jingzhou Prefecture, Huguang, was a prefectural government student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Jingfu, he ranked first in family order, and he was twenty-nine, born on the third day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Pu, his grandfather Botai, his father Lin, his mother née Zhao, and his stepmother née Zhuo; his grandparents and parents were living, he married a woman née Ai and subsequently a woman née Zhao, and he placed sixty-second in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 247th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Jin, registered in a salt-producing household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a county government student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Yuanpu, he ranked fiftieth in family order, and he was twenty-nine, born on the tenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wen; his grandfather Bing was posthumously appointed Secretary of the Guizhou Bureau in the Ministry of Justice; his father Xun was a Prefectural Vice Prefect; his mother, née Zhu, was posthumously granted the title Lady of Peace, and his stepmother, née Lu, was granted the same title. His parents were living; his elder brothers were Shimei, a medical official, Zhen 鎭, Fu, and Hua, and his younger brothers were Rong, Zhen 鎮, Lian, and Jin; he married a woman née Yin and placed seventy-ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 149th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Hui, registered in an official household of the Independent Battalion at Pingding Subprefecture, Shanxi, was a native of Huaiyuan County, Fengyang Prefecture, in the directly administered region; he specialized in the Book of Documents, his courtesy name was Baifu, he ranked eighth in family order, and he was twenty-four, born on the twenty-ninth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xi; his grandfather Feng was posthumously granted the rank Gentleman for Cultivated Service and the office of Prefectural Judge; his father Fang was Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief, and his mother, née Dong, was granted the title Lady. His parents were living; his elder brothers were Ji, Shen, Fu, Shou, Cai, and Ling, and his younger brothers were Wei and Yue; he married a woman née Yan and placed eighth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 131st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ji Cheng, registered in an artisan household in Kai Subprefecture, Daming Prefecture, in the directly administered region, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Jingfu, he ranked second in family order, and he was thirty-eight, born on the thirteenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xuan, his grandfather Lun, his father Chen, an Administrator, and his mother née Liu; his parents were living, his elder brother was Jian, and his younger brothers were Su, Shen, Fang, Zhen, Zhan, Fen, Qia, Chong, and Hao. He married a woman née Duan and subsequently a woman née Li, and placed eighty-fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 178th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Yan Tianxiang 嚴天祥 was registered in a military household in Chaoyi County, Tongzhou, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Shushan; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-one years old, born on the sixteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ke, his grandfather Feng, and his father Yaosi; his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Tianyou and Tianqi, and his wife was née Cao. He placed sixth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 252nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Jian 張鑑 was registered in a civilian household in Nanchong County, Shunqing Prefecture, Sichuan. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Ruming; he ranked fourth among his brothers and was thirty-six years old, born on the thirteenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Dagui. His grandfather Congzheng was posthumously granted the titles of Grand Master for Governance (fengzheng dafu) and Right Chief Administrator in the household of the Prince of Shu. His father Zhen was Right Chief Administrator in the same princely household and was advanced to rank 4a. His father’s former wife, née Li, was posthumously granted the title Lady of Suitability (yiren); his mother, née He, received the same title, and his stepmother was née Liu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Quan, Lian, Duo (a jinshi of the same examination cohort), and Yin; his younger brother was Xuan. His wife was née Wang; he subsequently married a woman née Chang and another née Wang. He placed fourteenth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 196th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Yingji 劉應箕 was registered in a civilian household in Ba County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Weinan; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-one years old, born on the twenty-second day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhongying, his grandfather Boquan, and his father Ao; his mother was née Yang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yingbi and Yingkui, and his wife was née Cao. He placed seventieth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 256th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gan Guan 甘觀 was registered in an official household of the Nanjing Palace Army Right Guard and was a native of Huaining County in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zhenfu; he ranked third among his brothers and was forty-one years old, born on the seventeenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather Jun was posthumously granted the title General of Manifest Might (mingwei jiangjun). His grandfather Jing was an Assistant Commander and was posthumously granted the title General of Illustrious Valor (zhaoyong jiangjun). His father was Quan, his mother was née Li, and his stepmother was née Zhang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Yu, an acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioner, and Lu; his younger brother was Wen. His wife was née Lu, and he subsequently married a woman née Sun. He placed 101st in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 263rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Gao Guang, courtesy name Ziqian, was registered in a military household in Emei County, Jiading Subprefecture, Sichuan. A county school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked fifth among his brothers and male cousins and was aged thirty-three, born on the twenty-fourth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yu; his grandfather, Lun; and his father, Shixian, an Imperial University student awarded a seventh-rank prestige title under the applicable regulations. His mother was née Xu and his stepmother née Yin; both parents were living. His elder brothers were Fu, Bi, Jie, and Shang, and his younger brother was Chang. His wife was née He. He placed thirty-fourth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 269th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Sikui, courtesy name Ruyi, was registered in a civilian household in Wujiang County, Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked second among his brothers and male cousins and was aged twenty-eight, born on the twenty-sixth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jun, holder of a seventh-rank prestige title; his grandfather, Xian, a subprefectural judge; and his father, Yi, an Imperial University student. His father's former wife was née Chen, his mother née Xu, and his stepmother née Lu. He had living parents and grandparents. His elder brother was Siyi; his younger brothers were Sigao, an Imperial University student, Siji, Sixie, and Silong. His wife was née Niu. He placed seventy-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 101st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Keyong, courtesy name Zicai, was registered in a civilian household in Yongfeng County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi. An attached student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked twenty-ninth among his brothers and male cousins and was aged twenty-eight, born on the thirteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gui, a vice prefect; his grandfather, Bing, a subprefectural clerk; and his father, Tai. His mother was née Lü. He had living parents and grandparents. His elder brother was Keliang, and his younger brothers were Kerang, Kezhong, Kejun, and Keqin. His wife was née Li. He placed fiftieth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 266th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Qian, courtesy name Yiqing, was registered in a civilian household in Pinghu County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first among his brothers and male cousins and was aged thirty-six, born on the eleventh day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ying; his grandfather, Zhen; and his father, Yi. His mother was née Pan; his father was deceased and his mother living. His wife was née Ma, and his subsequent wife née Zhang. He placed twenty-ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and ninety-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wan Cai, registered in Fengcheng County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a military household and was an additional student of the county school. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Yihe, and he ranked fifth in his family. He was twenty-eight, born on the nineteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Rongshu, his grandfather Jingfang, his father Hong, and his mother née Huang. His mother was living, and his father was deceased. His elder brothers were Chong, Kui (a provincial sacrificial official [?]), Hua, Sui (a provincial sacrificial official [?]), and Yuan. He married a woman née Xiong. He placed fifty-fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 304th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Xue, registered in Yangshuo County, Guilin Prefecture, Guangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Shigu, and he ranked third in his family. He was thirty-one, born on the sixth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Su (a Registrar), his grandfather Zuo, and his father Cheng (an Assistant Prefect); his mother was née Su, and his stepmother née Jiang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Qinxue and Haoxue, and his younger brothers Shixue, Wenxue, and Youxue. He married a woman née Rong. He placed thirty-ninth in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and 320th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Lian, registered in Wugong County, Qian Subprefecture, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Bochun, and he ranked tenth in his family. He was thirty-five, born on the twenty-fourth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Hai, his grandfather Rang, his father Ruzhen, and his mother née Kang. His mother was living, and his father was deceased. His elder brothers were Yingzhong, Yingxiang, Zhu, Yingqi, Yingzhen, Yue, Yinghe, and Ke (all tribute scholars, gongshi). He married a woman née Zhao. He placed forty-sixth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 287th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Kan belonged to a military household registered with Taihe Guard [?] in Zhili and was a native of Kunshan County, Suzhou Prefecture. He was a student of the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Record of Rites; his courtesy name was Xunqing, and he ranked first in his family. He was thirty-six, born on the nineteenth day of the intercalary ninth month. His great-grandfather was Qing, his grandfather Jing (an honorary official), and his father Gai (an honorary official); his father's principal wife was née Jin, and his birth mother née Qu. His mother was living, and his father was deceased. His elder brothers were Xian, Xiang, and Wei, and his younger brothers Xin, Biao, Gun (a student of the Directorate of Education), Xiang (a student of the Directorate of Education), and Xi. He married a woman née Xie and subsequently a woman née Shen. He placed forty-first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 158th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
He Haiyan 何海晏, courtesy name Zhixiang, was registered in a military household in Pingyin County, Dongping Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong. A county government student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first in birth order and was twenty-four years old, born on the sixteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tai, his grandfather Shu, and his father Qi; his father's principal wife was née Zhou, and his birth mother was née Si. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. He married a woman née Jiang. He placed twenty-fourth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 286th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ge Jue 葛桷, courtesy name Anfu, was registered in a civilian household in Shangyu County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first in birth order and was thirty-seven years old, born on the twenty-third day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenyu, posthumously granted the titles Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Minister of the Court of Judicial Review; his grandfather was Yongcheng, his father Pang, and his mother née Fan. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Mei, Mo (an honorary official), Mu (an Administration Vice Commissioner), and Xiang; his younger brothers were Qiang, Gai, Fei (a student of the Directorate of Education), and Nie (a student admitted by virtue of an official's privilege). He married a woman née Yu. He placed sixty-ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 180th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qian Shi 錢仕, courtesy name Zhongfu, was registered in a civilian household in Jiangling County, Jingzhou Prefecture, Huguang. A prefectural government student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first in birth order and was thirty-nine years old, born on the twenty-seventh day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xun, his grandfather Ning, and his father Fuzhen; his mother was née Hu, and his stepmother née Zhuang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Ji, Xiang, Ren, Ru, Xin, Yi, Dian, and Jun. He married a woman née Yan. He placed fourteenth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 268th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xue Zhang 薛樟, courtesy name Ziqiao, was registered in an artisan household in Licheng County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong. A county government student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked third in birth order and was thirty-two years old, born on the third day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Youde, his grandfather Sheng, his father Hu, and his mother née Cao. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Mei (an annual tribute student) and Nan. He married a woman née Zhang and subsequently married another woman née Zhang. He placed twelfth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 198th in the Metropolitan Examination.

陳甘雨〔貫福建興化府莆田縣，鹽籍，國子生，治詩經，字應時，行五，年二十九，二月十七日生〕。曾祖宏〔雅七品散官〕，祖世顯〔典史〕，父泉，前母林氏，母方氏。慈侍下，兄甘露，弟甘霖、甘瓠，娶黃氏。福建鄉試第二十九名，會試第二十八名。

席上珍〔貫四川潼川州遂寧縣，民籍，國子生，治春秋，字聘之，行一，年三十五，十一月二十三日生〕。曾祖祖憲〔封兵部郎中，贈光祿大夫、柱國、少保兼太子太保、禮部尚書兼武英殿大學士〕，祖書〔光祿大夫、柱國、少保兼太子太保、禮部尚書兼武英殿大學士，贈太傅，諡文襄〕，父中〔尚寶司卿〕，母楊氏〔贈宜人〕，繼母楊氏〔封宜人〕。具慶下，弟上寶、上賚、上儒、上卿、上士、上壽、上策、上簡、上廕、上吉、上應，娶趙氏。四川鄉試第十九名，會試第二百七十三名。
translation_en:
Gu Zhongxu, courtesy name Zisheng, was registered in Haifeng County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, in a civilian household. A county school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged twenty, and born on the second day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Wenyou; his grandfather, Qiang; and his father, Tong. His father's former wives were née Tang and née Liu, and his mother was née Men. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Yue, and his younger brother was Zhonghan. He married a woman née Yang. He ranked sixteenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and seventy-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ling Ruzhi, courtesy name Yunhu, was registered in Taicang Subprefecture, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a civilian household. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the fifth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Fang; his grandfather, Gao; his father, Kun; and his mother, née Chen. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Ruxue and Yunyi, the latter a tribute scholar (gongshi). He married a woman née Gu. He ranked forty-first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 251st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Ganyu, courtesy name Yingshi, was registered in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, in a salt-producing household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was fifth in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the seventeenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Hong, who held a seventh-rank prestige title [?]; his grandfather was Shixian, an unranked county official; and his father was Quan. His father's former wife was née Lin, and his mother was née Fang. His mother alone was living. His elder brother was Ganlu, and his younger brothers were Ganlin and Ganhu. He married a woman née Huang. He ranked twenty-ninth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and twenty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xi Shangzhen, courtesy name Pinzhi, was registered in Suining County, Tongchuan Subprefecture, Sichuan, in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the twenty-third day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather, Zuxian, was granted the title of Director in the Ministry of War and posthumously awarded the titles of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Pillar of State, Junior Guardian concurrently Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and Minister of Rites concurrently Grand Secretary of the Hall of Military Glory. His grandfather, Shu, held these latter titles and was posthumously awarded the title of Grand Preceptor and the name Wenxiang. His father, Zhong, was Chief Minister of the Office of Imperial Seals. His mother, née Yang, was posthumously awarded the title Lady of Suitability; his stepmother, also née Yang, was granted the same title. Both his father and stepmother were living. His younger brothers were Shangbao, Shanglai, Shangru, Shangqing, Shangshi, Shangshou, Shangce, Shangjian, Shangyin, Shangji, and Shangying. He married a woman née Zhao. He ranked nineteenth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 273rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Li Jiugong, registered in Yuzhou, Nanyang Prefecture, Henan, belonged to a military household and was a student of the department school. He specialized in the Classic of Changes; his courtesy name was Weixu, and he ranked second in birth order. He was aged thirty-four [?; the transcription has 生 in place of the expected 年], born on the twenty-first day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Hai, his grandfather Gui, and his father Yu; his mother was née Zhou and his stepmother née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Jiusi; his younger brothers were Jiuxu, Jiucheng, Jiugao, and Jiude. He married a woman née Yang. He placed twenty-seventh in the Henan Provincial Examination and 266th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Zongxing, registered in Yizhou, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a military household and was a student of the department school. He specialized in the Classic of Documents; his courtesy name was Jishan, and he ranked ninth in birth order. He was aged twenty-seven, born on the ninth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather Gang was posthumously granted the titles Grand Master for Aid in Governance and Right Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate. His grandfather Jing was Grand Master for Glorious Happiness, Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and Left Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate; he was posthumously granted the title Junior Guardian and the name Gongjing. His father Shiyan was a student of the Imperial University. His father's principal wife was née Jiang, and his birth mother née Guo. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Zongxian, an Office Deputy in the Court of Imperial Entertainments; Zongzhe, Zongwen, and Zongyou, holders of honorary official rank; Zongguan, a tribute scholar; Zongye; and Zongben. His younger brothers were Zongmin and Zongxun. He married a woman née Sun. He placed twenty-first in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 262nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Kongzhao, registered in Xingtai County, Shunde Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the county school. He specialized in the Classic of Changes; his courtesy name was Ziqian, and he ranked second in birth order. He was aged twenty-six, born on the seventh day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Ying, his grandfather Fang, and his father Yong; his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Kongyang, a student of the Imperial University, and Kongyi, a Sacrificial Attendant; his younger brother was Kongjia. He married a woman née Hao. He placed twelfth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 253rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Yonglu, registered in Changzhi County, Lu'an Prefecture, Shanxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the prefectural school. He specialized in the Record of Rites; his courtesy name was Shixue, and he ranked second in birth order. He was aged twenty-seven, born on the twenty-second day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather Ming was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi); his grandfather Zhang and father Mu were both Stewards of a princely household. His mother, née Chen, had received official recognition as a chaste widow. His family status was recorded as 'double celebration,' indicating surviving elders in the parental and grandparental generations. His elder brother Yongjue was a tribute scholar. He married a woman née Li. He placed first in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 280th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Chen Changyan, registered in a civilian household in Jieyang County, Chaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Defu; he was third in birth order, aged forty-nine, and born on the twenty-seventh day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Mengrong, his grandfather Jinbao, his father Lian, and his mother née Shi. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Changdai, and his wife was née Ji. He placed seventy-second in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 282nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Xuan, registered in a military household in Zhangqiu County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, was a county government school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yigong; he was third in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the twentieth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ding, his grandfather Pu (an honorary official honored for longevity), his father Ying (a County Magistrate), and his mother née Shi. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brothers were Jin and Dao, and his younger brothers Xun and Lian; his wife was née Zhao. He placed forty-first in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 234th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xiao Yi’e, registered in a civilian household in Xinyu County, Linjiang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Erjian; he was fifth in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the twenty-eighth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuanshang (posthumously appointed Registrar of a Guard), his grandfather Lianche, his father Lide, and his mother née Zhang. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Yiming, Yifeng, Yihuang, Yiyuan, and Yijiu. His wife was née Zhou; he subsequently married a woman née Zhang. He placed sixty-first in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 236th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang He, registered in a civilian household in Chang’an County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zigao; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the twenty-sixth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yan, his grandfather Jing, his father Luan, and his mother née Zhao. Both parents were living. His wife was née Zhou. He placed seventh in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and eighty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Shunde 王順德, courtesy name Shuchang, was registered in Luzhou, Sichuan, in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged forty-four, born on the eleventh day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xuan, his grandfather Chen, and his father Dacai; his mother was née Hua and his stepmother née Li. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Shunxian, and his wife was née Yang. He placed sixty-second in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 267th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Xizhou 黃希周, courtesy name Zonglu, was registered in Teng County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, in a military household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged forty, born on the eighth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Can; his grandfather Qi held an honorary official title for longevity; and his father Jin was Commissioner of the Chengyun Treasury. His mother was née Dong, and his stepmothers were née Men and née Sun. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Xiyan, Ximeng, Xizeng, and Ximin, and his wife was née Liu. He placed sixtieth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 309th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Feng Yinglin 馮應麟, courtesy name Deji, was registered in Fengxiang County, Fengxiang Prefecture, Shaanxi, in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Poetry, he ranked third among his brothers and was aged thirty-five, born on the thirteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yin; his grandfather Shou was a tribute scholar; and his father was Sheng. His father's former wife was née Fan, and his mother was née Dong. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brother was Yingqi, and his wife was née Wang. He placed twelfth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 308th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Chun 李淳, courtesy name Yanmu, was registered in Jiajiang County, Jiading Subprefecture, Sichuan, in a salt-producing household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged forty-five, born on the eighth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tingzuo, his grandfather Mo, and his father Guan, a Professor; his mother was née Zheng. His father was living and his mother deceased. His first wife was née Jiang, and his subsequent wife was née Wang. He placed twenty-first in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 175th in the Metropolitan Examination.
