translation_en:
Shen Sui, courtesy name Yiqing, was registered in a civilian household in Wei County, Daming Prefecture, in the Metropolitan Region, and was a native of Lucheng County, Shanxi. A county government school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was thirty-six years old, was born on the twenty-seventh day of the second lunar month, and had his birth order recorded as 三ニ [?]. His great-grandfather Zhu was a Registrar; his grandfather Qing was a Police Chief; his father was Qian, and his mother was née Wang. His father was living and his mother deceased. He married a woman née Li. He ranked seventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fifty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jiang Zhen, courtesy name Minpu, was registered in a military household in She County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the Metropolitan Region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was tenth in birth order, thirty-seven years old, and born on the thirtieth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yongzhen, his grandfather Wenhan, and his father Cai; his mother was née Zheng and his stepmother née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xiu, Pei, and Guan, the last a government school student; his younger brothers were Xuan and Lu. He married a woman née Wu. He ranked thirty-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 226th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Lan, courtesy name Yunshao, was registered in a civilian household in Licheng County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong. A county government school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was first in birth order, thirty-nine years old, and born on the fourth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rong, his grandfather Xianhui, and his father Ru; his legal mother was née Peng and his birth mother née Pang. His mother was living and his father deceased. He married a woman née Cao. He ranked sixty-seventh in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 291st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shi Jing, courtesy name Yingsheng, was registered in a civilian household in Yidu County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong. A prefectural government school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was eighth in birth order, twenty-eight years old, and born on the twenty-first day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather Ying was a Clerk; his grandfather Ming was a Prefectural Assistant Prefect, posthumously granted the rank of Grand Master for Forthright Service and the office of Vice Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue. His father Cunli was a Prefect, advanced to the rank of Grand Master for Exemplary Service. His legal mothers were née Jiang, granted the title Lady of Suitability, and née Liu; his birth mother was née Zhai. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Qi and Lin, both Imperial University students; Pu; Feng and Ju, both tribute students; Yu; and Huang. His younger brothers were Qu and Dong. He married a woman née Li. He ranked seventh in the Shandong Provincial Examination and twentieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Ma Kuai, courtesy name Ruli, was registered in a civilian household in Guangping County, Guangping Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A county-school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged twenty-nine, born on the twenty-fifth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xiang; his grandfather, Hong; his father, Zheng, an Assistant Instructor; and his mother, née Li. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Shen, and his wife was née Zheng. He placed sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 142nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Tingzhan, courtesy name Shouqing, was registered in a military household in Puzhou, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi. A department-school student specializing in the Classic of Documents, he ranked third among his brothers and was aged forty, born on the twenty-eighth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wei; his grandfather, Jian; his father, Xun; and his mother, née Gu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Tingmu and Tingsong, and his younger brother was Tingzi. His wife was née Liang; he subsequently married a woman née Li. He placed sixteenth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 134th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Bangyan, courtesy name Yunzhen, was registered in a civilian household in Huai'an County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian. An attached student of the county school specializing in the Classic of Changes, he ranked fifth among his brothers and was aged twenty-eight, born on the eighteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hua; his grandfather, Ming, a Jail Warden in the Provincial Surveillance Commission; his father, Tinghan; and his mother, née Lin. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His wife was née Lin. He placed forty-first in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 314th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jiang Tingyi, courtesy name Yizheng, was registered in a military household in Baling County, Yuezhou Prefecture, Huguang. A prefectural-school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-eight, born on the twenty-fifth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chun; his grandfather, Yongjun, posthumously appointed Registrar; his father, Yi, a government-school student granted the honor of wearing an official cap and girdle; and his mother, née Chen. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Tingze, Tingyong, Tinglai, Tinggu, and Tingyu. His wife was née Xie. He placed fifty-ninth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 157th in the Metropolitan Examination.

孫坊〔貫錦衣衛籍，浙江餘姚縣人，國子生，治易經，字志國，行六十，年二十九，五月二十三日生〕。曾祖孟宏〔贈禮部尚書〕，祖彬〔教諭〕，父煉，母鄭氏。具慶下，兄逹〔詹事府詹事兼翰林院學士〕、堪〔前母舉人中書舍人〕、墀〔光祿寺丞〕、陞〔翰林院編修〕、玨〔聽選官〕、佳〔貢士〕，弟埴。娶夏氏，繼娶姜氏。順天府鄉試第三十四名，會試第五十五名。

朱曰藩〔貫直隸揚州府高郵州寶應縣軍籍，國子生，治書經，字子价，行一，年四十四，六月十八日生〕。曾祖瓘，祖訥〔知縣，封戶部主事，進三品服〕，父應登〔布政司參政〕，母陶氏〔封安人〕。慈侍下，弟曰夔、曰蕋〔監生〕、曰蕙。娶茆氏。應天府鄉試第三十六名，會試第一百二十九名。

俞謹〔貫直隸常州府無錫縣民籍，國子生，治書經，字懋庸，行三，年四十一，七月二十二日生〕。曾祖允恭，祖純，父顯，母丁氏。永感下，兄武、文，弟斌。娶陳氏。應天府鄉試第九十六名，會試第二百八十九名。

李廷春〔貫四川重慶府江津縣軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字元甫，行四，年四十二，十月十九日生〕。曾祖璇，祖志昂，父林，前母胡氏，母劉氏，繼母劉氏。永感下，娶黃氏。四川鄉試第六名，會試第三百十二名。
translation_en:
Sun Fang, courtesy name Zhiguo, was registered with the Embroidered Uniform Guard and was a native of Yuyao County, Zhejiang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked sixtieth in his family’s birth order and was twenty-nine, born on the twenty-third day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather Menghong was posthumously granted the title of Minister of Rites; his grandfather Bin was a county school instructor; his father was Lian, and his mother was née Zheng. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Da, Household Administrator of the Household Administration of the Heir Apparent and concurrently Academician of the Hanlin Academy; Kan, a provincial graduate and Secretariat Drafter (the preceding words 前母, “former mother,” are unclear here [?]); Chi, Assistant Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments; Sheng, Compiler in the Hanlin Academy; Jue, an official awaiting selection for appointment; and Jia, a tribute scholar. His younger brother was Zhi. He married a woman née Xia and subsequently a woman née Jiang. He placed thirty-fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fifty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Yuefan, courtesy name Zijie, belonged to a military household registered in Baoying County, Gaoyou Subprefecture, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first in his family’s birth order and was forty-four, born on the eighteenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Guan; his grandfather Ne was a county magistrate, received the honorary title of Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue, and was granted the right to wear third-rank official dress. His father Yingdeng was an Administration Vice Commissioner in a Provincial Administration Commission; his mother, née Tao, held the title of Lady of Peace. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His younger brothers were Yuekui, Yuerui, an Imperial University student, and Yuehui. He married a woman née Mao. He placed thirty-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 129th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Jin, courtesy name Maoyong, belonged to a civilian household registered in Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked third in his family’s birth order and was forty-one, born on the twenty-second day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Yungong, his grandfather Chun, his father Xian, and his mother née Ding. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Wu and Wen, and his younger brother was Bin. He married a woman née Chen. He placed ninety-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 289th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Tingchun, courtesy name Yuanfu, belonged to a military household registered in Jiangjin County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked fourth in his family’s birth order and was forty-two, born on the nineteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Xuan, his grandfather Zhi’ang, and his father Lin. His father’s former wife was née Hu, his mother was née Liu, and his stepmother was also née Liu. Both parents were deceased. He married a woman née Huang. He placed sixth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 312th in the Metropolitan Examination.

郭公週〔貫福建福寧州福安縣，民籍，縣學生，治詩經，字景復，行六，年三十三，四月初八日生〕。曾祖克茂，祖惟盛，父允寧，母李氏。慈侍下，兄景調、景鳴，弟景聲、景芝、文賓，娶李氏，繼娶薛氏。福建鄉試第四十三名，會試第一百八名。
translation_en:
Li Rulan, registered in Xianning County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, belonged to an artisan household and was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Xiufu; he ranked second among his brothers, was twenty-nine years old, and was born on the twenty-sixth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yue, his grandfather Mei, and his father Yuchun; his mother was née Wang and his stepmother née Feng. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Ruzhi, and his younger brothers were Ruhui and Ruxuan. His wife was née Bai. He placed thirty-fifth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and eighty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Congshan, registered in Boping County, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Rudeng; he ranked second among his brothers, was thirty years old, and was born on the twenty-sixth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shixian, his grandfather Shan, and his father Zhao, Commissioner of Mingzhi Ward; his mother was née Fu. His grandparents and parents were living. His elder brother was Weishan and his younger brother Jishan. His wife was née Yang. He placed twentieth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 139th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jin Jiuling, registered in Wujin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yushou; his recorded birth-order rank was first, he was thirty-six years old, and he was born on the twelfth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hong, his grandfather Jun, and his father Huan; his mother was née Yang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Sheng and Xing; his younger brothers were Jiucheng, a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the same examination year, Jiugao, and Jiusi. His wife was née Chen. He placed fortieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 136th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guo Gongzhou, registered in Fu’an County, Funing Subprefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Jingfu; he ranked sixth among his brothers, was thirty-three years old, and was born on the eighth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kemao, his grandfather Weisheng, and his father Yunning; his mother was née Li. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Jingdiao and Jingming; his younger brothers were Jingsheng, Jingzhi, and Wenbin. His wife was née Li; he subsequently married a woman née Xue. He placed forty-third in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 108th in the Metropolitan Examination.

劉體乾〔貫直隸順天府東安縣民籍，縣學生，治禮記，字子元，行四，年三十三，十二月二十三日生〕。曾祖原，祖旺，父景〔教諭〕，嫡母馬氏、萬氏，生母高氏。慈侍下，兄榮、九思〔省祭官〕、九經〔陰陽官〕，娶張氏。順天府鄉試第五名，會試第四十名。

李萬實〔貫江西建昌府南豐縣民籍，國子生，治春秋，字少虛，行一，年三十五，正月初七日生〕。曾祖廷予〔衛經歷〕，祖淡〔縣丞〕，父柱，母黃氏，繼母揭氏。重慶下，娶黃氏。江西鄉試第十二名，會試第一百二十一名。
translation_en:
Zhu Youfu, registered in a civilian household in Haining County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zizhen; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged forty, born on the fourth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fang, his grandfather Guang, his father Ji, and his mother née Shen. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Youheng, Youjie, Youxiang, and Youguang; his wife was née Jiang. He placed seventy-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fifty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ma Rusong, registered in a civilian household in Dongguang County, Jingzhou Subprefecture, Hejian Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was originally from Lingqiu County, Shanxi. He was a county school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Jiefu; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged twenty-nine, born on the twenty-third day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jin, his grandfather Gao, his father Yaofu (a Station Master), and his mother née Yang. His parents and a grandparent were living. His wife was née Qu. He placed seventeenth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 189th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Tiqian, registered in a civilian household in Dong'an County, Shuntian Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a county school student specializing in the Record of Rites. His courtesy name was Ziyuan; he ranked fourth among his brothers and was aged thirty-three, born on the twenty-third day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuan, his grandfather Wang, and his father Jing (an Instructor). His legal mothers were née Ma and née Wan; his birth mother was née Gao. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Rong, Jiusi (a sacrificial official, shengjiguan), and Jiujing (an official of calendrical and divinatory studies, yinyangguan). His wife was née Zhang. He placed fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fortieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Wanshi, registered in a civilian household in Nanfeng County, Jianchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a National University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Shaoxu; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-five, born on the seventh day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tingyu (a Guard Command Record Keeper), his grandfather Dan (a County Vice Magistrate), his father Zhu, his mother née Huang, and his stepmother née Jie. His parents and a grandparent were living. His wife was née Huang. He placed twelfth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 121st in the Metropolitan Examination.

賀承光〔貫陝西西安府華州渭南縣軍籍，縣附學生，治詩經，字子謙，行一，年二十七，四月二十九日生〕。曾祖儒，祖倉〔封兵部主事〕，父府〔任兵部主事〕，母王氏〔封安人〕。具慶下，娶高氏。陝西鄉試第九名，會試第二百七十七名。

沈束〔貫浙江紹興府會稽縣民籍，府學生，治易經，字宗安，行十九，年三十一，四月十八日生〕。曾祖恪，祖琨，父藎〔知州〕，母張氏，繼母莊氏。具慶下，兄橋〔刑部主事〕、术、東、柬，弟蝀、秉、稟，娶張氏。浙江鄉試第一名，會試第一百二十六名。

translation_en:
He Chengguang, registered in a military household in Weinan County, Huazhou, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, was a supplementary student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Ziqian; he was first in birth order, aged twenty-seven, and born on the twenty-ninth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Ru; his grandfather, Cang, received the honorary title of Secretary in the Ministry of War; his father, Fu, served as Secretary in the Ministry of War; and his mother, née Wang, received the title of Lady of the Sixth Rank (anren). Both parents were living. He married a woman née Gao. He placed ninth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 277th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Shu, registered in a civilian household in Kuaiji County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zong’an; he was nineteenth in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the eighteenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Ke; his grandfather was Kun; his father, Jin, was a Department Magistrate; his mother was née Zhang, and his stepmother was née Zhuang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Qiao, a Secretary in the Ministry of Justice, Shu (术) [?], Dong, and Jian; his younger brothers were Dong (蝀), Bing (秉), and Bing (稟). He married a woman née Zhang. He placed first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 126th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Su Zhiren, registered in a military household in Haiyang County, Chaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Daoxian; he was second in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the twenty-ninth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Jing; his grandfather was Yi; his father was Siyi; his father’s former wife was née Zheng, and his mother was née Xu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Zhixue, and his younger brothers were Zhigu and Zhixin. He married a woman née Qiu. He placed eighteenth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and seventy-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Ziqiang, registered in a civilian household in Fugou County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Tiqian; he was second in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the third day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather, Xian, was an honorary official; his grandfather, Rui, was a District Magistrate; his father, Dong, was an Imperial University student; and his mother was née Fan. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother, Zixiu, was an annual tribute student; his younger brothers were Zide, Ziren, Zixiu (自秀), Zicun, and Zili. He married a woman née Li. He placed sixty-seventh in the Henan Provincial Examination and 179th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wu Chang 吳昶, courtesy name Boming, was registered in the military banner register of Dengzhou Guard, Shandong, and was a native of Taizhou in Zhili; an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked first among his brothers, was forty-five years old, and was born on the twenty-seventh day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yong, his grandfather Zhen, his father He, and his mother née Ni; his father was deceased and his mother living; his younger brother was Zhang, and his wife was née Ding; he placed fifty-sixth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and three hundred tenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Maoju 林懋舉, courtesy name Zhiqing, was registered as a civilian in Huai’an County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, and was a native of Min County; an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Changes, he ranked third among his brothers, was thirty-five years old, and was born on the ninth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ying, his grandfather Kui, his father Jiong, and his mother née Deng; both parents were deceased; his younger brothers were Maozhong, Maoyu, Maocai, Maoxiu, Maogong, and Maozhang, and his wife was née Gong; he placed thirty-seventh in the Fujian Provincial Examination and ninety-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Ti 張禔, courtesy name Jiefu, was registered as a civilian in Xiangfu County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan; a prefectural school student specializing in the Classic of Documents, he ranked second among his brothers, was thirty-four years old, and was born on the fifteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Mu, his grandfather Liang, his father Mingde, and his mother née Tian; his father was deceased and his mother living; his elder brother was Qi, his younger brother Zhi, and his wife was née Wang; he placed forty-ninth in the Henan Provincial Examination and two hundred thirtieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ren Xizu 任希祖, courtesy name Yuanxiao, was registered as a civilian in Cangxi County, Baoning Prefecture, Sichuan; a prefectural school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked first among his brothers, was thirty-four years old, and was born on the twenty-fifth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bin, a Department Magistrate; his grandfather was Mo, his father Zhongren, his father’s former wife née Li, and his mother née Wang; both parents were living; his younger brothers were Jizu, Shengzu (a tribute scholar, gongshi), Zuanzu, Shuaizu, and Fazu, and his wife was née Xiang; he placed thirty-fifth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and two hundred third in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Ji Lian 冀鍊, courtesy name Chunfu, was registered in Yidu County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, in a civilian household. A National University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked second in birth order and was thirty-two years old, born on the second day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wendao; his grandfather, Kun; his father, Jiujing, a County School Instructor; and his mother, née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Duan. He married a woman née Zhang and subsequently a woman née Song. He placed fifteenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and ninety-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tu Zemin 塗澤民, courtesy name Zhiyi, was registered in Hanzhou, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, in a civilian household. A department school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first in birth order and was twenty-three years old, born on the tenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kui; his grandfather, Wanlong; his father, Lun; and his mother, née Wen. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Jimin, and he married a woman née Gu. He placed eighteenth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 106th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Duan Xiu 叚繡, courtesy name Wengui, was registered in Gu'an County, Shuntian Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a civilian household. A National University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked second in birth order and was thirty-nine years old, born on the tenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ji; his grandfather, Buzhi, a District Magistrate; and his father, Gong, a Relay Station Master. His mother was née Gao, and his stepmother was née Han. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brother was Jin; his younger brothers were Yue, Lian (a Secretary in the Ministry of Works), Chun, Kai, and Rui. He married a woman née Yi. He placed ninetieth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 231st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Wenlin 李文麟, courtesy name Yingzhen, was registered in Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a military household. A National University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked third in birth order and was thirty-four years old, born on the twelfth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tai, an honorary official recognized for longevity and posthumously granted the title of Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice. His grandfather was Cheng, a Director in the Ministry of Works, promoted to the prestige title Chaolie dafu. His father was Wei, and his mother was née Guo. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Wensheng, Wenfeng, Wenzhu, Wenheng, and Wenlong; his younger brother was Wenpeng. He married a woman née Wang. He placed fifty-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fifty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Hu Weizhong, courtesy name Kejiu, was registered in a civilian household in Gao’an County, Ruizhou Prefecture, Jiangxi. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the sixteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rui, granted the title of Supervising Secretary; his grandfather was Zhen, Assistant Administration Commissioner in the Zhejiang Provincial Administration Commission; his father was Song, authorized under established precedent to wear official cap and girdle; and his mother was née Fu. He had living grandparents and parents. His elder brothers were Weining and Weijing; his younger brothers were Weili, a tribute scholar, Weizhi, and Weizhe. His wife was née Shan. He placed forty-eighth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and seventy-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Yue, courtesy name Zongtai, was registered in a civilian household in Wujin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and was a native of Wuxi County. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the twenty-ninth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qing; his grandfather was Yuan, an honorary official recognized for charitable contributions; his father was Dajing, a Ceremonial Usher; and his mother was née Lu. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brother was Song, an Imperial University student; his younger brothers were Yan 巗, an Imperial University student, Yan 巖, a Clerk, Qin, Yin, Ya, and Cen. His wife was née Liu. He placed ninety-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 171st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xie Dang, courtesy name Xianzhong, was registered in a military household in Shangyu County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the nineteenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhu; his grandfather was E; and his father was Zuo. His father’s former wife was née Shen, his mother was née Xia, and his stepmother was née Gu. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Mi and Shi; his younger brothers were Tuo, Yingyan, and Xie. His wife was née Xu. He placed seventy-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 114th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Mu, courtesy name Ziqiao, was registered in a civilian household in Changshu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Rites, he was second in birth order, aged forty-one, and born on the twenty-sixth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shu; his grandfather was Bing; his father was Yin, a Secretary in the Ministry of Works; his mother was née Zou; and his stepmother was née Tang. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brother was Dong, a Sacrificial Attendant (shengjiguan); his younger brother was Ben. He married a woman née Zou and subsequently married women née Lu and née Li. He placed sixty-second in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and ninety-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

郝鳴陰〔貫順天府通州寶坻縣，民籍，縣學生，治書經，字子和，行一，年三十二，四月十二日生〕。曾祖倫，祖欽〔壽官〕，父喻〔歲貢生〕，母孟氏，繼母邵氏。重慶下，兄良棟、良佑、鳴遠，弟鳴亮，娶田氏。順天府鄉試第八十一名，會試第八十九名。

邵漳〔貫浙江紹興府餘姚縣，民籍，縣學生，治禮記，字子清，行二，年三十二，二月二十二日生〕。曾祖蕡〔贈監察御史〕，祖蕃〔提學副使，前提學御史，封孺人〕，父時順〔知縣〕，母來氏〔封孺人〕。重慶下，兄稷〔同科進士〕、濰，弟潢、淄、澐、澹、洲，娶胡氏。浙江鄉試第四名，會試第二百七名。

楊廷相〔貫雲南臨安衛，軍籍，直隸金壇縣人，國子生，治易經，字燮甫，行二，年三十二，六月初四日生〕。曾祖昇，祖儉，父均〔教授〕，母夏氏。具慶下，兄廷芳、廷春、環、塤、廷璧、珎，娶劉氏。雲南鄉試第六名，會試第二百六十一名。
translation_en:
Liu Jia 劉檟 was registered in Shanyin County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a military household. A student of the National University, he specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Yuanmei; he ranked twenty-sixth in family order and was thirty-two sui, born on the fourth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qi, his grandfather Jian, and his father Zhuo; his father's former wife was née Tian, and his mother was née Hu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Dong (Vice Minister of War at Nanjing), Ben (County School Instructor), Ji (tribute student), Jiao, Li, Rong, and Wu; his younger brother was Zhen. He married a woman née Yao. He placed fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and twenty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hao Mingyin 郝鳴陰 was registered in Baodi County, Tongzhou, Shuntian Prefecture, in a civilian household. A county government school student, he specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zihe; he ranked first in family order and was thirty-two sui, born on the twelfth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lun, his grandfather Qin (holder of an honorary official title conferred for longevity), and his father Yu (annual tribute student); his mother was née Meng, and his stepmother was née Shao. He had living grandparents and parents. His elder brothers were Liangdong, Liangyou, and Mingyuan; his younger brother was Mingliang. He married a woman née Tian. He placed eighty-first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shao Zhang 邵漳 was registered in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household. A county government school student, he specialized in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Ziqing; he ranked second in family order and was thirty-two sui, born on the twenty-second day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fen (posthumously appointed Investigating Censor), his grandfather Fan (Education Intendant with the rank of Vice Commissioner, formerly an Education Intendant with censorial rank; the annotation also says “granted the title Lady,” apparently misplaced [?]), and his father Shishun (District Magistrate). His mother, née Lai, was granted the title Lady. He had living grandparents and parents. His elder brothers were Ji (a metropolitan graduate in the same examination cohort) and Wei; his younger brothers were Huang, Zi, Yun, Dan, and Zhou. He married a woman née Hu. He placed fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 207th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Tingxiang 楊廷相 was registered in Lin'an Guard, Yunnan, in a military household, and was a native of Jintan County in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the National University, he specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Xiefu; he ranked second in family order and was thirty-two sui, born on the fourth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sheng, his grandfather Jian, and his father Jun (Prefectural School Instructor); his mother was née Xia. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Tingfang, Tingchun, Huan, Xun, Tingbi, and Zhen. He married a woman née Liu. He placed sixth in the Yunnan Provincial Examination and 261st in the Metropolitan Examination.

徐洛〔貫河南開封府許州軍籍，州學生，治詩經，字子京，行二，年三十四，八月二十五日生〕。曾祖學〔壽官〕，祖富〔典史〕，父綬〔醫官〕，母黄氏。嚴侍下，兄湯，弟汴。娶吳氏。河南鄉試第五十九名，會試第二百九十九名。

姚一元〔貫浙江湖州府長興縣軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字惟貞，行二，年三十六，五月初十日生〕。曾祖正，祖嶽〔知縣〕，父良輔〔歲貢生〕，母游氏。慈侍下，兄一夔，弟一暘、一鳴、一清、一瀾。娶錢氏。浙江鄉試第十二名，會試第二百二十一名。

鄭河〔貫應天府江寧縣民籍，江西新建縣人，國子生，治易經，字師程，行二，年三十四，九月二十八日生〕。曾祖思恭，祖禮〔知府〕，父珉〔封監察御史〕，嫡母歐陽氏〔封孺人〕，母生丁氏。慈侍下，兄濂〔按察司副使〕，弟渠。娶丁氏，繼娶丁氏。應天府鄉試第五十九名，會試第一百十名。
translation_en:
Bian Xun, registered in an official household in Renqiu County, Hejian Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Wenyun; he was fourth in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the seventh day of the third month. His great-grandfather Quan and grandfather Hong were both company commanders; his father Wei was a Salt Distribution Commissioner, and his mother, née Liu, held the title Grand Lady. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Shi, a company commander, Qing, and Pu; his younger brother Hang was a prefect. He married a woman née Min and subsequently a woman née Zhu. He placed ninetieth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 181st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Luo, registered in a military household in Xuzhou, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, was a student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zijing; he was second in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the twenty-fifth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather Xue held an honorary official title for longevity; his grandfather Fu was a clerk, and his father Shou was a medical officer. His mother was née Huang. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brother was Tang, and his younger brother was Bian. He married a woman née Wu. He placed fifty-ninth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 299th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yao Yiyuan, registered in a military household in Changxing County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Weizhen; he was second in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the tenth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Zheng; his grandfather Yue was a county magistrate, and his father Liangfu was an annual tribute student. His mother was née You. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Yikui; his younger brothers were Yiyang, Yiming, Yiqing, and Yilan. He married a woman née Qian. He placed twelfth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 221st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng He, registered in a civilian household in Jiangning County, Yingtian Prefecture, and originally from Xinjian County, Jiangxi, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Shicheng; he was second in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the twenty-eighth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Sigong; his grandfather Li was a prefect, and his father Min was granted the title Investigating Censor. His father's principal wife, née Ouyang, was granted the title Lady; his birth mother was née Ding [?—the transcription reverses the characters for “birth mother”]. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother Lian was a vice commissioner of a Provincial Surveillance Commission; his younger brother was Qu. He married a woman née Ding and subsequently another woman née Ding. He placed fifty-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 110th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Yizhong, registered in an artisan household in She County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Zhengshu, he was second in birth order, and he was aged thirty, born on the thirtieth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Longsheng, his grandfather Fuchen, his father Wenxian, and his mother Lady Fang; both parents were living. His elder brother was Yiguan, and his younger brother Yicheng was a student of the Directorate of Education. He married Lady Cheng and placed sixteenth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventeenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Yanzhong, registered in a civilian household in Jurong County, Yingtian Prefecture, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Rujing, he was third in birth order, and he was aged thirty-nine, born on the twenty-first day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Zhihai, his grandfather Zhen, his father Zonglun, and his mother Lady Zhu; his mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Yanwen and Yanwu, and his younger brothers Yanxiao, Yanfang, Yanrong, Yanxi, Yanque, and Yanbo. He married Lady Qiao and placed eighty-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fifty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Shen, registered in an officer household of the Baoding Right Guard under the Daning Regional Military Commission and originally from Wu’an County, Henan, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Yongxiu, he was first in birth order, and he was aged thirty, born on the eighteenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Zhen, his grandfather Lian and his father Jing were both company commanders, and his mother was Lady Jia; his parents and grandparents were living. He married Lady Liu and placed twenty-eighth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and two hundred eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Gang, registered in a military household in Xingguo Subprefecture, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Lizhi, he was first in birth order, and he was aged thirty-four, born on the twenty-seventh day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Junxian, his grandfather Bihua, his father Xinghan, his father’s former wife Lady Li, and his mother Lady Huang; his mother was living and his father deceased. He married Lady Cheng and placed twenty-second in the Huguang Provincial Examination and sixty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

牛珠〔貫河南開封府通許縣，匠籍，國子生，治易經，字光甫，行一，年四十三，三月二十日生〕。曾祖春，祖增，父杲，母李氏，繼母安氏。慈侍下，弟璜，娶藺氏。河南鄉試第三十五名，會試第二百七十九名。

林應奎〔貫福建漳州府龍溪縣，軍籍，府學附學生，治易經，字德暉，行二，年三十，十月初二日生〕。曾祖啓昭，祖體用，父泰，母傅氏。具慶下，兄應元，弟應祥，娶吳氏，繼娶張氏。福建鄉試第五十三名，會試第一百四十六名。

王之誥〔貫湖廣荆州府石首縣，軍籍，縣學生，治書經，字告若，行十二，年三十三，十一月初八日生〕。曾祖俸〔七品散官〕，祖伯載，父芳〔同知〕，母曾氏。慈侍下，兄之誠，弟之度、之紀、之綱、之惠，娶劉氏。湖廣鄉試第七十六名，會試第二百九十四名。
translation_en:
Chen Xin, registered in Shangyu County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, in an artisan household, was a county government student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zixing, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was forty years old, born on the twelfth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Jingfu, his grandfather was Rumian, a tribute student, his father was Dalian, and his mother was née Zhu; both parents were living; his elder brother was Zuo, a District Magistrate, and his younger brothers were Ren, Ji, Xi, and Jiang, the last a metropolitan graduate of the same examination cohort; his wife was née Gong; he placed thirty-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fifteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Niu Zhu, registered in Tongxu County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, in an artisan household, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Guangfu, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was forty-three years old, born on the twentieth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Chun, his grandfather was Zeng, his father was Gao, his mother was née Li, and his stepmother was née An; his father was deceased and his mother living; his younger brother was Huang, and his wife was née Lin; he placed thirty-fifth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 279th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Yingkui, registered in Longxi County, Zhangzhou Prefecture, Fujian, in a military household, was an attached student of the prefectural government school specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Dehui, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was thirty years old, born on the second day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Qizhao, his grandfather was Tiyong, his father was Tai, and his mother was née Fu; both parents were living; his elder brother was Yingyuan and his younger brother was Yingxiang; his wife was née Wu, and his subsequent wife was née Zhang; he placed fifty-third in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 146th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Zhigao, registered in Shishou County, Jingzhou Prefecture, Huguang, in a military household, was a county government student specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Gaoruo, he ranked twelfth among his brothers, and he was thirty-three years old, born on the eighth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Feng, a prestige official of the seventh rank, his grandfather was Bozai, his father was Fang, a Vice Prefect, and his mother was née Zeng; his father was deceased and his mother living; his elder brother was Zhicheng, and his younger brothers were Zhidu, Zhiji, Zhigang, and Zhihui; his wife was née Liu; he placed seventy-sixth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 294th in the Metropolitan Examination.

石茂華〔貫山東青州府益都縣，民籍，府學生，治詩經，字君采，行二，壬二十三，七月初九日生〕。曾祖銘〔府通判，贈奉直大夫、南京戶部員外郎〕，祖存禮〔知府，進階中憲大夫〕，父麒，嫡母公氏，生母張氏。具慶下，弟茂藻、茂貞，娶戈氏。山東鄉試第二十九名，會試第二百十六名。

宋賢〔貫直隸松江府華亭縣，竈籍，國子生，治春秋，字及甫，行一，年三十九，六月初八日生〕。曾祖鍇，祖玉，父蕙，母吳氏。重慶下，弟士、使、卿、相，娶金氏。應天府鄉試第二十二名，會試第十六名。

趙宸〔貫直隸保定府定興縣，民籍，國子生，治書經，字德聰，行二，年二十九，正月初二日生〕。曾祖剛，祖讓，父自，母張氏。慈侍下，兄寅，弟宇、宦，娶馬氏。順天府鄉試第一百二十一名，會試第四十九名。

高鏞〔貫四川成都府內江縣，民籍，國子生，治書經，字景甫，行二，年三十三，九月初九日生〕。曾祖友恭〔知縣，贈通議大夫、戶部右侍郎〕，祖齊南〔府通判，贈承德郎，加贈通議大夫、戶部右侍郎〕，父公韶〔通議大夫、戶部右侍郎〕，前母冉氏〔贈孺人，加封淑人〕，母羅氏〔封孺人，加封淑人〕。具慶下，兄麒〔太僕寺丞〕、岡〔給事中〕、材〔光祿寺署丞〕、蔭、恩〔官生〕、鈺、鉞〔歲貢生〕、錬〔國子生〕、鈞〔監生〕，弟鐈、銓、鑑、錥、鏜〔監生〕，娶鄭氏，繼娶喻氏。四川鄉試第四十九名，會試第二百十七名。
translation_en:
Shi Maohua, registered in Yidu County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a civilian household and was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Juncai; he ranked second in birth order, was aged twenty-three [?; the transcription has 壬 in place of the expected 年], and was born on the ninth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather Ming was a prefectural Assistant Administrator, posthumously granted the title Grand Master for Upright Service and the office of Vice Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue; his grandfather Cunli was a Prefect, advanced to Grand Master for Central Rectitude. His father was Qi, his legal mother was née Gong, and his birth mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Maozao and Maozhen, and his wife was née Ge. He placed twenty-ninth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 216th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Song Xian, registered in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered region, belonged to a salt-producing household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Jifu; he ranked first in birth order, was aged thirty-nine, and was born on the eighth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kai, his grandfather Yu, his father Hui, and his mother née Wu. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Shi, Shi, Qing, and Xiang (士、使、卿、相), and his wife was née Jin. He placed twenty-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Chen, registered in Dingxing County, Baoding Prefecture, in the directly administered region, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Decong; he ranked second in birth order, was aged twenty-nine, and was born on the second day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gang, his grandfather Rang, his father Zi, and his mother née Zhang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Yin, his younger brothers were Yu and Huan, and his wife was née Ma. He placed 121st in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and forty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gao Yong, registered in Neijiang County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Jingfu; he ranked second in birth order, was aged thirty-three, and was born on the ninth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather Yougong was a District Magistrate, posthumously granted the title Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and the office of Right Vice Minister of Revenue. His grandfather Qinan was a prefectural Assistant Administrator, posthumously granted the title Gentleman for Receiving Virtue and subsequently the title Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and the office of Right Vice Minister of Revenue. His father Gongshao was Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Right Vice Minister of Revenue. His father's former wife, née Ran, was posthumously granted the title Lady for Service, subsequently raised to Lady of Virtue; his mother, née Luo, was granted the title Lady for Service, subsequently raised to Lady of Virtue. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Qi, Assistant Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud; Gang, Supervising Secretary; Cai, Assistant Office Director in the Court of Imperial Entertainments; Yin and En, followed by the annotation ‘student admitted by virtue of official ancestry’; Yu and Yue, followed by ‘annual tribute student’; Lian, an Imperial University student; and Jun, an Imperial University student. His younger brothers were Qiao, Quan, Jian, Yu, and Tang, followed by the annotation ‘Imperial University student.’ His wife was née Zheng; he subsequently married a woman née Yu. He placed forty-ninth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 217th in the Metropolitan Examination.

張守直〔貫順天府薊州遵化縣民籍，國子生，治禮記，字時舉，行三，年二十九，六月二十七日生〕。曾祖成，祖士能〔知縣，進階六品〕，父繼〔本州吏目〕，嫡母王氏，生母高氏。慈侍下，兄希載、希戢，弟守簡、希儒、守約，娶李氏，繼娶趙氏。順天府鄉試第四十四名，會試第二百五十名。

周世遠〔貫四川重慶府江津縣民籍，縣學附學生，治詩經，字子道，行二，年二十五，九月十八日生〕。曾祖瑄，祖玉鑑〔壽官〕，父謨，母何氏。具慶下，兄世才，弟世表、世業，娶楊氏。四川鄉試第五十四名，會試第五十七名。
translation_en:
Jin Zhe, registered in a civilian household in Dongyang County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Rudong; he ranked twenty-third in his family and was aged thirty, born on the seventh day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Zongfeng, his grandfather Bang, his father Qiu, and his mother née Xu. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Pu, Yuan, and He. He married a woman née Xuan and subsequently a woman née Xu. He placed seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 177th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cheng Zixue, registered in a military household in Haiyang County, Chaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Huaidao; he ranked fourth in his family and was aged forty-two, born on the eighteenth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Shang, his grandfather Yin, his father Hu, and his mother née Cai. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Zijun, Zijie, and Ziyou. He married a woman née Hong. He placed eleventh in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 112th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Shouzhi, registered in a civilian household in Zunhua County, Jizhou, Shuntian Prefecture, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Shiju; he ranked third in his family and was aged twenty-nine, born on the twenty-seventh day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Cheng; his grandfather, Shineng, was a county magistrate advanced to the sixth rank; and his father, Ji, was a clerk of Jizhou. His father's principal wife was née Wang, and his birth mother was née Gao. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Xizai and Xiji; his younger brothers were Shoujian, Xiru, and Shouyue. He married a woman née Li and subsequently a woman née Zhao. He placed forty-fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 250th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Shiyuan, registered in a civilian household in Jiangjin County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, was an attached student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zidao; he ranked second in his family and was aged twenty-five, born on the eighteenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Xuan; his grandfather, Yujian, held an honorary official title awarded for longevity; his father was Mo, and his mother née He. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Shicai, and his younger brothers were Shibiao and Shiye. He married a woman née Yang. translation_en:
Ma Ruji, registered in an official household of Jinzhou Guard under the Liaodong Regional Military Commission, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Defu; he ranked third among his brothers, was aged twenty-seven, and was born on the first day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xiong (an honorary official for longevity), his grandfather Zhao, his father Ang (an Assistant Prefect), and his mother née Liu. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brothers were Ruxian, Ruzhi, and Chaozong (an Assistant Commander); his younger brothers were Rulong, Rucong, and Ruhua. His wife was née Sun. He placed eighty-seventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 151st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cai Yangjin, registered in a military household of the Thousand-household Office in Weihui Prefecture, Henan, was originally from Xingan County, Jiangxi. He was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zili; he ranked second among his brothers, was aged thirty-two, and was born on the eighth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xing, his grandfather Run, his father Jingyu, and his mother née Huang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Nanjin, and his wife was née Yang. He placed seventy-fourth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 300th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Peng Yinglin, registered in a civilian household of Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a county government school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Taifu; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged forty-one, and was born on the twelfth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wen, his grandfather Zhong, and his father Rong; his father's former wife was née Zhang, and his mother was née Feng. Both parents were deceased. His wife was née Zhou. He placed sixteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 132nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fu Qing, registered in a military household of Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, was originally from Puqi County, Huguang. He was a prefectural government school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Xianqing; he ranked fifth among his brothers, was aged thirty-five, and was born on the nineteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ruxian, his grandfather Tan, and his father Ziyan; his father's former wife was née He, and his mother was née Fang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Kai, Ti, Nan, and Xiang; his younger brother was Maochun. His wife was née Ruan. He placed sixty-first in the Fujian Provincial Examination and fifty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Sun Xuegu, registered in an artisan household in Xiaoshan County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Rusui, he ranked third in birth order, and he was aged thirty, born on the fourth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Xin, a seventh-rank prestige official; his grandfather was Shi, an honorary official; his father was Huan, an official awaiting selection for appointment; his mother was née Cai and his stepmother née Zhou; his father was still living, but his mother had died; his elder brothers were Xuesi, a Secretariat Drafter, and Xueli; his wife was née Zhang; he placed eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and sixty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ma Zhenzhang, registered in a civilian household in Liyang County, Yingtian Prefecture, Nanjing, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Guohua, he ranked fifth in birth order, and he was aged forty, born on the third day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Meng, his grandfather Yongqing, his father Su, and his mother née Yang; both parents were deceased; his younger brother Zhenyan was an Imperial University student; his wife was née Shi; he placed fifty-seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Chengzu, registered in a civilian household in Licheng County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Kexiu, he ranked first in birth order, and he was aged twenty-nine, born on the third day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Gui, a Commissioner; his grandfather was Xian, a Surveillance Vice Commissioner; his father was Chun and his mother née Lu, both still living; his younger brother was Chengye; he married a woman née Gao and subsequently a woman née Si; he placed first in the Shandong Provincial Examination and three hundred thirteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yan Qing, registered in a military household of the Yunnan Rear Guard and originally from Jiaxing County, Zhejiang, was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Zhiqing, he ranked third in birth order, and he was aged twenty-one, born on the eighteenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Liang, his grandfather Hao, his father Ying, and his mother née Yu; his parents and grandparents were living; his elder brothers were Ji, Han, Zhi, Xue, Yu, Zhan, Chun, Run, Zhang, Su, and Zhou, and his younger brothers were Zi and Shan; his wife was née Shi; he placed thirty-sixth in the Yunnan Provincial Examination and one hundred sixty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

His great-grandfather was Run, his grandfather Hui, and his father Jin, an Assistant Instructor; his mother was née Cui. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Xian, Yu, Yi, Cai, and Mi. He married a woman née Liu. He placed thirty-second in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and nineteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Shu, registered in a civilian household in Xian County, Hejian Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a county government school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Daofu; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-two, born on the eighth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gui, his grandfather Jian, and his father Zong; his mother was née Yu. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Ying. He married a woman née Tang. He placed fifty-fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 185th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Gonglin, registered in a civilian household in Kaihua County, Quzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a county government school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Juzhi; he ranked fifth among his brothers and was aged thirty-one, born on the twelfth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Mian, an honorary official recognized for longevity; his grandfather was Xi, an honorary official recognized for righteousness; his father was Wencan, and his mother was née Yu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Gongjian, Gongxuan, Gonglu, Gongxi, and Gongwang. He married a woman née Yu and subsequently a woman née Shi. He placed twenty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 161st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wei Wenyang, registered in a military household in Houguan County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, and a native of Fuqing County, was a prefectural government school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Dezhang; he ranked sixth among his brothers and was aged thirty, born on the twenty-eighth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was An, his grandfather Zhenqing, and his father Duo, an honorary official recognized for longevity. His father's principal wife was née Chen, and his birth mother was née Hu. His parents were living. His elder brothers were Wenhuan, a tribute scholar (gongshi), Wencan, and Wenbing. He married a woman née Zheng and subsequently a woman née Gao. He placed forty-ninth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and forty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Guo Bangguang, registered in Guan County, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a military household and was a county school student. He specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yuanbin; he ranked second among his brothers and was twenty-eight years old, born on the sixteenth day of the intercalary first month. His great-grandfather was Min; his grandfather, Lun, was an unranked clerk; his father, Ding, was an associate prefect; and his mother was née Cao. His parents and grandparents were deceased. His elder brother, Bangxian, was an Imperial University student. He married a woman née Xu. He placed sixty-second in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 238th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Bangyan, registered in Changzhi County, Lu’an Prefecture, Shanxi, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student. He specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Dechong; he ranked third among his brothers and was forty-three years old, born on the fifteenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Qi, his grandfather Ying, his father Fu, and his mother née Liu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Bangzhong and Bangjie, the latter an Imperial University student; his younger brothers were Bangqi, Bangyi, Bangzhao, and Bangli. He married a woman née Shen. He placed fifty-ninth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 214th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Han Chaojiang, registered in Liquan County, Qian Subprefecture, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, belonged to a military household and was an Imperial University student. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Shunfu; he ranked third among his brothers and was forty-five years old, born on the first day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Ying; his grandfather, Ming, held an honorary official title for longevity; his father was Zhang; and his mother was née Yang. His parents and grandparents were deceased. His elder brothers were You and Ziyu [?]; his younger brothers were Chaohu, Linjiang, Chaoxun, an Imperial University student, and Chaohuai. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed third in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 184th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Xingke, registered in Jianli County, Jingzhou Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a military household and was a county school student. He specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zishu; he ranked second among his brothers and was twenty-eight years old, born on the twenty-fifth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Yu, his grandfather Renshou, his father Qi, and his mother née Li. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brother was Xingjian; his younger brothers were Xingfu and Xingshi. He married a woman née Zhou. He placed seventy-second in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 319th in the Metropolitan Examination.

His great-grandfather was Rang, his grandfather Yanming, and his father Xuan, a Chief Clerk; his mother was née Chen. Both parents were deceased. His great-grandfather was Xuanben, his grandfather Sheng, and his father Rong; his mother was née Xu. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Zhang. His great-grandfather was Simin, his grandfather Zhao, and his father Xuan; his mother was née Tang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Fu, and his younger brothers were Ke and Han. He married a woman née Zhu. He ranked thirty-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and eighty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zuo Dan, registered in Dazu County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a military household and was an additional student at the county school specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Junfa; he was first in birth order, aged twenty-seven, and born on the fifteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Boxun, his grandfather Wandi, and his father Lijiao; his mother was née Liang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Ang, Ding, and Xian. He married a woman née Zhou. He ranked twenty-second in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 272nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

何尚賢〔貫山西平陽府猗氏縣監籍，縣學生，治春秋，字汝思，行二，年三十二，七月初八日生〕。曾祖濟〔鴻臚寺序班〕，祖純，父廷璋，母張氏。慈侍下，兄尚德〔知州〕，娶張氏，繼娶王氏。山西鄉試第六十名，會試第一百五十名。

李尚智〔貫山西潞安府屯留縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字汝愚，行一，年二十七，九月二十日生〕。曾祖友，祖綱，父世雷，母趙氏。慈侍下，兄尚仁，弟尚信、尚矩，娶郝氏，繼聘尹氏。山西鄉試第三十二名，會試第二百二十四名。
translation_en:
Yang Yingyuan, courtesy name Boren, was registered with the Herds Office (Qunmu Suo) in Shaanxi and came from Xiaoshan County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. He was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, third in family order, aged thirty-four, and born on the sixth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Mengqing, his grandfather Wan, his father Hu, and his mother née Hu. His mother alone was living. His elder brothers were Yingsong and Yingsu, and his younger brother was Jie. He married a woman née Fan. He placed forty-sixth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and one hundredth in the Metropolitan Examination.

You Ying, courtesy name Rubai, belonged to a military household in Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. He was a county government student specializing in the Book of Documents, seventh in family order, aged thirty-four, and born on the nineteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qian, his grandfather Yue, and his father Jin; his father's former wife was née Zhu, and his mother was née Hua. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Lian, Zhuo, Bi, Xun, Lin, and Huan; his younger brothers were Chen, Gong, Li, Ai, Xuan, Fan, and Jue. He married a woman née Qian. He placed first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twelfth in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Shangxian, courtesy name Rusi, was registered in Yishi County, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, under a directorate registration category (jianji) [?]. He was a county government student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, second in family order, aged thirty-two, and born on the eighth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ji, an Usher in the Court of State Ceremonial; his grandfather was Chun, his father Tingzhang, and his mother née Zhang. His mother alone was living. His elder brother Shangde was a department magistrate. He married a woman née Zhang and subsequently a woman née Wang. He placed sixtieth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and one hundred and fiftieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Shangzhi, courtesy name Ruyu, belonged to a civilian household in Tunliu County, Lu'an Prefecture, Shanxi. He was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, first in family order, aged twenty-seven, and born on the twentieth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was You, his grandfather Gang, his father Shilei, and his mother née Zhao. His mother alone was living. His elder brother was Shangren, and his younger brothers were Shangxin and Shangju. He married a woman née Hao and was subsequently betrothed to a woman née Yin. He placed thirty-second in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and two hundred and twenty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

梁恩〔貫湖廣岳州府巴陵縣，軍籍，縣學生，治詩經，字子承，行七，年二十九，五月十三日生〕。曾祖文達，祖志澄，父原千，母許氏，生母黎氏。慈侍下。兄崏、崘、岳、爵、俊、冕。娶廖氏。湖廣鄉試第五十一名，會試第二百八十一名。

張逵〔貫浙江紹興府餘姚縣，官籍，國子生，治易經，字懋德，行十二，年三十二，二月十七日生〕。曾祖皞，祖僅，父珊，母史氏。永感下。兄遷、逹〔刑科右給事中〕、迪、遜〔監生〕、遠、遴、建〔貢士〕，弟選。娶吳氏。浙江鄉試第五十七名，會試第六十三名。
translation_en:
Hu Zhikui, registered in a salt-producing household in Anyi County, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Minghe; he was third in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the twenty-ninth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Mincong; his grandfather, Rui, was a county magistrate; and his father, Zhen, was an Imperial University student. His father's former wife was née Lu, and his mother was née Wen. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Zhigao and Zhitai, and his younger brother was Zhilong. He married a woman née Guo and subsequently married another woman née Guo. He placed forty-fifth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 188th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Yue, registered in a platoon commander's household in the Central Battalion of the Chengdu Left Escort Guard, Sichuan, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Jiyuan; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the twelfth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather, Kuan, held an honorary longevity title; his grandfather was Jingyuan, his father was Sen, and his mother was née Han. Both parents were deceased. He married a woman née Wang. He placed forty-fourth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 232nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liang En, registered in a military household in Baling County, Yuezhou Prefecture, Huguang, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zicheng; he was seventh in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the thirteenth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Wenda, his grandfather was Zhicheng, and his father was Yuanqian. His mother was née Xu, and his birth mother was née Li. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Min, Lun, Yue, Jue, Jun, and Mian. He married a woman née Liao. He placed fifty-first in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 281st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Kui, registered in an official household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Maode; he was twelfth in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the seventeenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Hao, his grandfather was Jin, his father was Shan, and his mother was née Shi. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Qian; Da, Right Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Justice; Di; Xun, an Imperial University student; Yuan; Lin; and Jian, a Metropolitan Examination graduate (gongshi). His younger brother was Xuan. He married a woman née Wu. He placed fifty-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and sixty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Shoumeng, courtesy name Qizhe, was registered in a military household in Teng County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, and was originally from Huayin County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the nineteenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sheng, his grandfather Huan, his father Zhao, and his mother née Fu. His grandfather and both parents were living. His younger brothers were Shouxun, Shouxun (守巽), and Shouheng; his wife was née Dang. He placed thirteenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 227th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Jingshao, courtesy name Zicheng, was registered in a military household in Chongyang County, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang. A supplementary student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes, he was third in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the third day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Duo, his grandfather Shaoji, and his father Jin; his father's principal wife was née Gan, and his birth mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jingming and Jingfang, and his younger brothers Jingguang and Jingzhong; his wife was née Zhang. He placed sixtieth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 267th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Hualu, courtesy name Jirong, was registered in a civilian household in Xiangfu County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the tenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lin; his grandfather Wei held an honorary official title for longevity; his father Run was a School Instructor; and his mother was née Fu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Guanlu, Zailu, Bianlu, and Xinglu; his wife was née Jia. He placed fifteenth in the Henan Provincial Examination and eighty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Luo Wenwei, courtesy name Bianfu, was registered in a civilian household in Qijiang County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-nine, and born on the tenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jian, his grandfather Tianliang, his father Min, and his mother née Sun. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Wenjiao and Wenxun; his wife was née Meng. He placed thirtieth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 113th in the Metropolitan Examination.

李初元〔貫四川順慶府營山縣，民籍，縣學生，治易經，字少貞，行一，年二十六，正月十五日生〕。曾祖仕麒〔主簿〕，祖鏊，父渾然，母任氏。具慶下，弟慶元、亨元、體元，娶陳氏。四川鄉試第四十七名，會試第一百七十六名。

王國光〔貫山西澤州陽城縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字汝觀，行二，年三十三，十二月初一日生〕。曾祖子文〔義官〕，祖禹，父承祖，母原氏，繼母曹氏、張氏。具慶下，兄重光，弟爭光、前光、奎光、近光、耿光，娶張氏，繼娶衛氏。山西鄉試第十九名，會試第一百九十四名。

趙祖元〔貫浙江金華府東陽縣，民籍，縣學生，治詩經，字宗仁，行六十三，年二十三，三月十八日生〕。曾祖太錦〔監生〕，祖為濂，父繼宋，母吳氏。具慶下，兄祖庶，弟祖朝、祖臺、祖薦，娶劉氏。浙江鄉試第九十名，會試第三十名。

朱寵〔貫湖廣武昌衛後千戶所，官籍，山東兗州府寕陽縣人，國子生，治詩經，字德承，行三，年三十二，七月十六日生〕。曾祖瑛〔千戶〕，祖璽〔千戶〕，父金〔千戶〕，母張氏〔封宜人〕。具慶下，兄官〔千戶〕、寅，娶李氏，繼娶劉氏。湖廣鄉試第五十四名，會試第二百三十五名。
translation_en:
Li Chuyuan, registered in Yingshan County, Shunqing Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Shaozhen, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was twenty-six years old, born on the fifteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shiqi, a Registrar; his grandfather was Ao; his father was Hunran; and his mother was née Ren. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Qingyuan, Hengyuan, and Tiyuan, and his wife was née Chen. He placed forty-seventh in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 176th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Guoguang, registered in Yangcheng County, Zezhou, Shanxi, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Ruguan, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was thirty-three years old, born on the first day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ziwen, an honorary official; his grandfather was Yu; his father was Chengzu; his mother was née Yuan; and his stepmothers were née Cao and née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Chongguang, and his younger brothers were Zhengguang, Qianguang, Kuiguang, Jinguang, and Gengguang. His wife was née Zhang, and he subsequently married a woman née Wei. He placed nineteenth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 194th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Zuyuan, registered in Dongyang County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zongren, he ranked sixty-third in his family’s birth order, and he was twenty-three years old, born on the eighteenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Taijin, an Imperial University student; his grandfather was Weilian; his father was Jisong; and his mother was née Wu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Zushu, and his younger brothers were Zuchao, Zutai, and Zujian. His wife was née Liu. He placed ninetieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and thirtieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Chong, registered in an official household of the Rear Battalion of Wuchang Guard, Huguang, was originally from Ningyang County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Decheng, he ranked third among his brothers, and he was thirty-two years old, born on the sixteenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather Ying, grandfather Xi, and father Jin were all Battalion Commanders; his mother, née Zhang, had been granted the title Lady of Suitability. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Guan, a Battalion Commander, and Yin. His wife was née Li, and he subsequently married a woman née Liu. He placed fifty-fourth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 235th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Zishun, registered in an official household of Dezhou Guard in the Metropolitan Region and a native of Tang County, Henan, was a student of the department school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Jufu, and he ranked second in his family; the age notation is garbled, apparently indicating thirty-five [?]. He was born on the seventeenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Ji, his grandfather Ning, and his father Pei; his mother was née Wu and his stepmother née Xu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Zixiao, and his younger brothers were Zihua and Zipan. His wife was née Xia. He placed fifth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 264th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Ren, registered in a civilian household of Qimen County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the Metropolitan Region, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Ziren, and he ranked fifteenth in his family. He was thirty years old, born on the fourteenth day of the intercalary fourth month. His great-grandfather was Hongdao, his grandfather Ruhong, and his father Jie; his mother was née Xie. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Beng, and his younger brother Mou. His wife was née Hu. He placed sixty-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and tenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yin Congjian, registered in an official household of Guilin Right Guard, Guangxi, was an added student of the Guilin prefectural school specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Ruzhong, and he ranked first in his family. He was twenty-six years old, born on the twenty-first day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Wang, his grandfather Xiong, and his father Zan; his mother was née Huang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Jie, a company commander, and Feng; his younger brother was Congyi. His wife was née Qin. He placed sixth in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and 316th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qiu Shilian, registered in a civilian household of Sheng County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zixian, and he ranked thirty-eighth in his family. He was thirty years old, born on the twenty-fifth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Zhun, his grandfather Zong, a government school student, and his father Yuelin; his mother was née Zhang and his stepmother née Li. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brothers were Shiyu, Shiqi, Shipei, and Shibian. His wife was née Xing. He placed seventy-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fourteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.
